zh:
陈三生平没遇上过这般难缠的对手。
阿爹教给他们的那些本事，讲究一个快字。往往三息之内，便足以吓退他们所有的对手。
但面前这男人，以退为进，化守为攻，几个来回间，竟渐渐摸着了他们的命门。

是的，命门。他陈三不是什么无懈可击的怪物，他只是由三个娃娃装神弄鬼扮成的骗子。
骗子的破绽，并不难找。他们节节败退，但他们不能认输。因为他们是阿爹手中的一把武器。
武器存于世，若不能替主人赢来胜利，便只能被遗弃。为了不被遗弃，他们只能拼命往前，永不停歇。
这便是他们在这个比武场内，学到的人世的道理。

最后一掌击过来时，站在小七肩膀上的小八认命的闭上了眼。
兜兜转转，他们还是走回了那被遗弃的命运。
但那强有力的掌风，却在他的脸侧停下了。
小八睁眼，见那人扬着一张笑脸，而后掌心上翻，露出里头的一颗由红色糖衣包裹的糖果。
“我认输。”突起的烟雾中，那男人倏地自顾自倒地，扬声高喊。
en:
Chen San had never faced such a stubborn opponent.
The tricks their father taught them relied on speed. Within three breaths, they'd usually scare off any rival.
But this man used retreat as advance, turning defense into attack. In mere moments, he'd already found their weak spot.

Yes, weak spot. Chen San wasn't an unbeatable monster, just three children masquerading as a ghostly fraud.
Finding a con artist's flaw wasn't hard. They were losing ground, but they couldn't admit defeat. They were their father's weapon.
A weapon that failed its master would be discarded. To survive, they had to fight on, never stopping.That was the first truth they'd learned in these bloody pits.

As the final palm strike came, Xiaoba, standing on Xiaoqi's shoulders, closed her eyes resignedly.
After all their struggles, abandonment was their fate.
But the deadly wind of the strike halted just beside her face.
Xiaoba opened her eyes to see the man grinning, palm upturned to reveal a red-wrapped candy.
"I yield." In a burst of smoke, the man dramatically collapsed onto his back, shouting his surrender to the roaring crowd.

zh:
开运三年，天泉弟子何具足既殁，未几，少年阿破的脸上现其故颜，宛然复生。
洛神之技出神入化，大到廓势肌理，小到痣点纹丝，都还原得纤毫毕现。
阿破从铜镜中照见自己如今的样子，愣怔了很久……他扯动嘴角挤出一个故作爽朗的笑容，竟然已经有九分像何具足了。
至于剩下的那一分——一道狰狞可怖的伤疤从眉头贯穿整个左眼，停留在脸颊上。血痂脱落不久，伤口处翻出粉白的新肉……还没有完全长好。
洛神站在一旁端详着他，语气淡漠：你明日便走吧，不必等它痊愈了。
阿破不明所以：为什么？
洛神微不可闻地叹了口气：伤口太深，即便是何具足活了下来，这道疤也长不好了。
冥冥之中似有天意，阿破为了躲避追杀自伤左颊，何具足阵前亦伤左颊……同庚同伤，宛如符契。

当夜，洛神的船夫撑着长篙，把阿破送出了弱水岸。船夫看看他，叹口气，看看他，又叹口气，摸出几块碎银，雇了几个脚夫，把他一路抬回了天泉。
亡命日久，食不果腹，本该扛鼎拔山的少年，如今形容枯槁，历经长途跋涉后，更是新伤摞旧伤……及至到了天泉山门处，几乎骸骨支离，人鬼莫辨。
北地苦寒，阿破脸上的伤口渗了血又结了霜，看上去极其惨烈。
他仰面躺在何具足生前的寝室，眼前蒙着一团血雾，影影绰绰地看到一个两鬓斑白的人影向他走来。
从旁边弟子的口中，他听见了“沈把头”三个字，心中有些疑惑：何具足明明跟他说过，沈寒英年纪不大，怎么会是这副满头华发的模样？
沈寒英查看了他的伤势，吩咐一位师兄照顾他的起居直至痊愈，自此再无赘言。
……有那么一刻，阿破几乎可以肯定，她已经认出自己是冒牌货了……可是，沈寒英到底还是什么也没说，只是沉默地坐在他的身边，一直守到了子夜。
夜里寒风刺骨，像不久前那三百弟子的死讯一样侵蚀着她。阿破闻到她身上金铁护具的腥寒，像雪，也像血。
两个跌入枯缝里的幸存者，无话可说，唯有缄口，等待死亡的余威平息。
……磨砖作镜，炊沙为饭，总好过万念俱灰。
阿破不知道沈寒英是什么时候离开的，不过他知道，他安全了。
他睡了沉沉的一觉，梦里没有见到哥哥，没有见到仇人，也没有见到逃亡路上的满地饿殍，遍野哀鸿……日光倾城，东风飒飒，他和何具足策马并辔走在初遇的山崖边……那是太平盛世里的他们，没人上战场，没人当流民。
走着走着，何具足消失了，走着走着，他变成了何具足。
翌日，他苏醒过来，惊讶地发现窗外的风声停了，与昨夜梦里一样的日光洒落在他脸上。
他恍惚记起，今日似乎是立春。
“青春受谢,白日昭只。”
——照顾他饮食起居的师兄在一旁翻动着手中的书页，将上面的内容郑重其事地念给他听，仿佛这是一个尚未公开、无人知晓的秘密。
en:
In the third year of Kaiyun, shortly after the Well of Heaven disciple He Juzu perished, the youth Po bore the dead man's visage upon his own face, as if the fallen had returned to life.
The Water Lady's disguise techniques were truly sublime. From the broad contours and muscle textures to the tiniest moles and pores, every detail was recreated with absolute precision.
Gazing at his current appearance in the bronze mirror, Po stared blankly for a long time. He forced his mouth to stretch into a feigned hearty smile; shockingly, he now bore a nine-tenths resemblance to He Juzu.
As for the remaining one-tenth: a ghastly, terrifying scar ran from his brow, tearing straight through his left eye, and settled upon his cheek. The blood scab had recently fallen off, revealing tender, pale-pink flesh. It had not yet fully healed.
Standing aside, the Water Lady observed him with a detached tone, telling him he should depart tomorrow and need not wait for the wound to heal.
Po was bewildered, asking why.
The Water Lady let out an almost imperceptible sigh, explaining that the wound was too deep; even if He Juzu had survived, this scar would never have fully healed.
It seemed the heavens had ordained a mystical parallel. Po had mutilated his own left cheek to evade pursuit, and He Juzu had suffered a strike to his left cheek on the battlefield. Born in the same year, bearing the exact same wound; it was as if dictated by a destined pact.
That night, the Water Lady's boatman pushed his long pole, ferrying Po away from the Still Shore. The boatman looked at him and sighed, then looked again and sighed once more. He fished out a few pieces of broken silver, hired some porters, and had Po carried all the way back to the Well of Heaven.
Having been a fugitive for so long, enduring endless starvation, the youth who was once strong enough to lift a cauldron was now reduced to a gaunt shadow. After surviving the grueling trek, his body was a canvas of new wounds layered over old. By the time he arrived at the mountain gates of the Well of Heaven, he was practically a disjointed skeleton, barely distinguishable from a ghost.
The bitter cold of the North caused the wound on Po's face to bleed and freeze over repeatedly, leaving him looking utterly tragic.
He lay flat on his back in the bedchamber that had once belonged to He Juzu. Through a bloody mist clouding his vision, he faintly saw a figure with greying temples approaching him.
From the lips of a disciple nearby, he heard the title "Chief Shen." A sliver of doubt arose in his heart: He Juzu had explicitly told him that Shen Hanying was quite young. How could she appear with a head full of white hair?
Shen Hanying examined his wounds, instructed a senior brother to attend to his daily needs until he recovered, and spoke not a single superfluous word thereafter.
For a fleeting moment, Po was almost certain she had recognized him as an imposter. Yet, in the end, Shen Hanying said absolutely nothing. She merely sat in silence by his side, keeping watch until the stroke of midnight.
The piercing night wind bit to the bone, gnawing at her much like the recent news of the three hundred disciples' deaths. Po could smell the metallic, cold scent of blood on her armor; it smelled like snow, and it smelled like blood.
Two survivors who had plummeted into the dry crevices of despair had nothing to say to one another. They could only remain silent, waiting for the aftershocks of death to subside.
Grinding a brick to make a mirror, cooking sand to make rice; futile as it may seem, it is still better than having all hopes turn to ashes.
Po did not know when Shen Hanying left, but he knew he was safe.
He fell into a deep, heavy slumber. In his dream, he did not see his brother Zhi, he did not see his enemies, nor did he see the starving corpses and wailing refugees that littered his path of exile. Instead, the sunlight flooded the city, and the spring wind rustled brightly. He and He Juzu were riding side by side along the cliff where they first met. It was the two of them in an era of peace, where no one had to march to war, and no one was reduced to a refugee.
As they rode on, He Juzu vanished. As he rode on, he became He Juzu.
The next day, he awakened, astonished to find that the howling wind outside the window had ceased. The exact same sunlight from his dream spilled across his face.
In a daze, he remembered that today seemed to be the Start of Spring.
"Spring takes its turn, and the bright sun shines clearly."
The senior brother tasked with his care was turning the pages of a book nearby, reading the text aloud with solemn reverence, as though reciting a profound secret yet to be unveiled to the world.
What lady...?

【笛】

箜篌引

卢溪郡南夜泊舟，夜闻两岸羌戎讴。
其时月黑猿啾啾，微雨沾衣令人愁。
有一迁客登高楼，不言不寐弹箜篌。

有一迁客登高楼，不言不寐弹箜篌。

公无渡河

黄河西来决昆仑，咆哮万里触龙门。
波滔天，尧咨嗟。
大禹理百川，儿啼不窥家。

en:
【Music·II】

【Flute】

Hearing a Flute on the Frontier
By Gao Shi
Snow melts, barbarian skies clear, horses return from pasture;
Moon bright, a Qiang flute sounds between the watchtowers.
I ask where the "Plum Blossom" tune will fall tonight;
The wind blows it all night long, filling the mountain passes.

Hearing a Flute on a Spring Night in Luoyang
By Li Bai
From whose house comes the secret flight of jade flute notes,
Scattering into the spring breeze, filling Luoyang?
Tonight in this melody I hear "The Broken Willow Branch";
Who would not feel, for native land, a rising homesick pang?

Playing the Flute
By Du Fu
Playing the flute on autumn hills, wind clear, moon bright;
Whose house crafts such heart-rending sounds with such skill?
The wind carries the pitch-pipes' harmonious strains so true;
The moon leans near the mountain passes, shining in several places.
Barbarian horsemen at midnight could head north in flight;
Thinking of southern campaigns, a tune from Wuling comes to mind.
Willows in my old garden now are withered, falling;
How can, amid such sorrow, a melody be fully born?

【Konghou (Harp)】

Konghou Prelude
By Wang Changling
Moored at night south of Luxi County,
I hear songs from both banks, Qiang and Rong tribes.
The moon is dark then, monkeys chirp and cry,
A light rain dampens clothes, stirring sorrow in the heart.
A banished traveler climbs a high tower,
Wordless, sleepless, he plays the konghou.
He plays of autumn mulberry leaves at Jimen Pass,
Of rustling wind and sand atop the green burial mounds.
The general's iron steed sweats blood,
Deep into Xiongnu lands, the battle never ceases.
A banished traveler climbs a high tower,
Wordless, sleepless, he plays the konghou.
He plays of autumn mulberry leaves at Jimen Pass,
Of rustling wind and sand atop the green burial mounds.
The general's iron steed sweats blood,
Deep into Xiongnu lands, the battle never ceases.

Do Not Cross the River, Sir
By Li Bai
The Yellow River comes west, bursting through the Kunlun Mountains,
Roaring for ten thousand li, striking the Dragon Gate.
Waves reach the sky; Yao sighs in dismay.
Great Yu regulated a hundred rivers,
His child cried, but he did not look home.
He checked the torrents, stemmed the floods,
And the Nine Provinces began to raise silkworms and hemp.
The harm was gone, leaving only vast, empty wind and sand.
An old man with loose hair, mad and foolish,
At dawn by the stream—what does he intend to do?
Others show no pity, his wife tries to stop him,
"Do not cross the river, sir!" yet he struggles to cross.
A tiger can be fought, a river cannot be trusted;
The old man indeed drowns, his body drifts to the sea's edge.
There is a long whale with white teeth like a snowy mountain;
Oh sir, oh sir, you are caught and tangled among them!
The konghou's lament is that he never returns.

Li Ping Plays the Konghou
By Li He
Wu silk, Shu paulownia strung in high autumn,
Empty mountains, congealed clouds sag and cease to flow.
River goddesses weep among bamboos, the plain maid grieves,
As Li Ping in the Middle Kingdom plays the konghou.
Jade of Kunlun shatters, phoenixes cry,
Lotus flowers weep dew, fragrant orchids smile.
Before the twelve city gates, cold light melts away;
Twenty-three strings move the Purple Emperor on high.
Where Nüwa smelted stones to mend the sky,
Stones split, heaven startled, provoking autumn rain.
Dreaming, he enters divine mountains, teaches an immortal crone;
Old fish leap in waves, gaunt water dragons dance.
Wu Gang, sleepless, leans against the cassia tree;
Dew-feet slanting fly, dampening the cold hare.

zh:

「风雷赛」采用公平调平模式，游侠可自由搭配武学、心法与奇术，数值不受角色养成影响（角色使用统一固定数值，武学为95级，心法为6重，奇术为6重9段，装备套装、调律及定音效果不生效）,挑战开始后可在准备阶段切换武学搭配和天工开物。

海选赛中游侠需依次挑战3名指定首领（海选赛为「寄棺主」「无名将军」「伊刀」），每名首领拥有3次挑战机会，当前首领全部挑战完成后，方可解锁下一名首领，取3次挑战中的最短用时作为该首领最优成绩，且该成绩使用的两个武学都将被锁定，禁止在后续挑战中重复使用，最终总成绩为三名首领最优成绩的用时总和。

淘汰赛中游侠需需连续挑战三名固定首领（淘汰赛为「「寄棺主」」「无名将军」「伊刀」），单次挑战内血量与药品数量全程继承不重置，且不同首领需使用完全不同的武学（仅单次挑战内限制），每个首领准备阶段可通过培养和背包切换武学及天工开物，共3次挑战机会，最终取最短用时作为成绩。

决赛的挑战规则同淘汰赛，最后一名首领决赛当日公布。
en:
Players must abide by Where Winds Meet General Tournament Rules. See the "General Tournament Rules" section on the official Where Winds Meet Tournament Center website. 

"Tempest" uses a Fair Level Adjustment Mode. Wanderers can freely customize Skills, Inner Ways, and Mystic Skills. Stats are not affected by character progression (characters use unified fixed stats; Martial Arts Level 95, Inner Ways Tier 6, Mystic Skills Tier 6 Stage 9; Gear Sets, Tuning, and Attunement effects are inactive). After the challenge starts, you can switch Skill loadouts and Divinecraft during the preparation phase.

In the Qualifiers, players must challenge 3 designated Bosses in order ("Puppeteer - Overture", "Nameless General", "Yi Dao"). Each Boss has 3 challenge attempts. You can only unlock the next Boss after completing the challenge for the current one. The shortest time among the 3 attempts is recorded as the best result; the Martial Arts combination used for this best result will be locked and cannot be reused in subsequent Boss challenges. The total score is the sum of the best times for all three Bosses.

In the Elimination Stage, players must consecutively challenge three fixed Bosses (Elimination Bosses: "Coffin Master", "General Nameless", "Yi Dao"). HP and medicine counts are inherited throughout the single run and do not reset. Completely different Martial Arts must be used for different Bosses (restriction applies only within a single run). Martial Arts and Divinecraft can be switched via Training and Bag during each Boss's preparation phase. Combat starts automatically after preparation. There are 3 challenge attempts, with the shortest total time taken as the final score. 

The Finals follow the same rules as the Elimination Stage. The final Boss will be announced on the day of the Finals.

zh:
我似乎记得，公主走的那一天，凉州根本没有下雪。
她将我们留在了别鹤居，独自一个人走向了望乡台。
明珠担心她，要为她掌灯，但她却摇手拒绝。
她是那么怕黑的一个人，夜夜都要持灯入睡。可她却说，她要去那座名为望帝乡的高塔上，找到能够映出回家路的月亮。

我们担心她，又不敢违逆她的意思，只好一步一步跟着她去。
我们跟着她漫步过醇香的酒池，登上延绵的雪山，又目送她款款走进望乡台。
那天的月光真美，好像能洗去她鬓间的风霜。

一袭白衣的公主唯有一支步摇傍身。她说她很抱歉，让我们也成为了和她一样的失乡人。
可我们又怎么会怨她呢。若没有她，我们早已冻死在遮天盖地的风雪中。
我见她登上名为望帝乡的高塔，轻轻伸手，拨开了浅浅的雾。
那一轮月亮，终于肯照亮她回家的路。
月光如银瓶乍破，从她的眉间发梢向尘世涌来。那光汇聚在池底，又溢满了望乡台。
公主的身影在倾泻的月光中浮现。我分明看到，她身后的层层宫阙鳞次栉比，似一朵牡丹盛放。她在月光中起舞翩跹，恰如未出阁时的明丽。我们也提起裙摆，蹚着月光，环绕在她身边击节而舞，彩袖飘摇。
她的影子，长安的影子，我的影子，都碎在一处，又被月光酿成了涟漪，漾出了一夜的盛唐。
我看到手上的皱纹缓缓平复，而我们的眉间却慢慢凝出晶莹的风霜。月光真冷啊，冷得人骨髓里都结冰。

哦，如此说来——
我似乎是记错了。公主走的那天，凉州下了很大很大的雪。
en:
I seem to remember that on the day the princess left, Liangzhou wasn't snowing at all. 
She left us at Crane Retreat and walked alone towards Hometown Tower. 
Mingzhu worried about her and wanted to hold a lantern for her, but she waved her hand in refusal. 
She was someone so afraid of the dark, needing to hold a lamp to sleep every night. Yet she said she was going to that high tower named Hometown Tower to find the moon that could illuminate the road home. 

We were worried but dared not disobey her, so we could only follow her step by step. 
We followed her strolling past the fragrant wine pool, climbing the endless snow-capped mountains, then watched her gracefully enter Hometown Tower. 
The moonlight that day was truly beautiful, as if it could wash away the frost and wind from her temples. 

The princess, dressed in white, only wore a hairpin. She said she was sorry for making us exiles like herself. 
But how could we blame her? Without her, we would have frozen to death in the overwhelming snowstorm long ago. 
I watched as she climbed the tower called Hometown Town, gently stretching out her hand to brush away the thin mist. 
At last, the moon was willing to light her way home. 
The moonlight gushed forth like a shattered silver vase, flowing from her brows and hair to the mortal world. The light gathered at the bottom of the pond, then filled the entire Hometown Tower. 
The princess's figure emerged in the pouring moonlight. I clearly saw layers of imperial palaces behind her, row upon row, like a blooming peony. She danced gracefully in the moonlight, as bright and beautiful as she was before marriage. We also lifted our skirts, waded through the moonlight, surrounded her, and danced to the rhythm, our colorful sleeves fluttering. 
Her shadow, Chang'an's shadow, my shadow, all shattered together, then brewed into ripples by the moonlight, rippling forth the glory of the prosperous Tang for one night. 
I watched the wrinkles on my hands slowly fade, yet crystal-clear frost gradually formed between our brows. The moonlight was so cold, cold enough to freeze one's bones. 

Oh, so it seems... 
I must have remembered wrong. The day the princess left, Liangzhou had a very, very heavy snowfall.

zh:
中渡桥一役，林险生与萧鹤衣并肩拒敌。是夜月晦星沉，桥下水声如咽。二人且战且退，眼见同袍殒落，旌旗没于烽火，胸中块垒难浇。
鹤衣仗剑断后，险生扶伤相护。刀光迫近之际，二人忽生默契，进退之间宛如一人双影。其一剑走龙蛇，大开大合；其一剑如游丝，尽锁要害。及至绝境，二人生死相托，剑光交织如茧，敌刃难近半分。
虽则后来林险生身染奇毒，此生仅剩三剑之力，然江湖论剑，天下推首，世人仰止处，仍是林萧并肩之名。
此术既成绝响，自当年之战后，风云寂寥，再无一人得见其锋芒。唯月明之夜，或闻双元居后两声剑鸣如诉，似在追忆那场生死与共的旧事。
武元当全力出剑，令文元此生不必全力再出一剑。
en:
At the Battle of Zhongdu Bridge, Lin Xiansheng and Xiao Heyi stood shoulder to shoulder against their foes. That night, the moon was dark, and the stars sank low. The waters beneath the bridge choked and sobbed. The two fought and retreated in turn, watching their comrades fall one by one. Blazing flames swallowed the banners, lodging a knot of grief deep within their chests that could not be washed away.
Heyi guarded the rear with his sword, while Xiansheng shielded him despite being wounded. As the flash of blades drew near, the two suddenly moved as one, advancing and retreating like a single soul cast in twin shadows. One stroke, bold and sweeping, as if a dragon has descended; another flows like a trailing thread, sealing every vital point. In their most desperate hour, the two entrusted their lives to one another, their sword-light interweaving like a cocoon, through which no blade could pass.
Though Lin Xiansheng later fell to a strange poison, leaving him strength for but three strikes of the sword for the rest of his days, still, in the discourse of swordsmanship across the jianghu, the names of these two were held above all others.
Years passed, the world calmed. That technique became a swan song, leaving none to behold it once more. Only on nights of the full moon might one hear, behind the Essence Retreat, two cries of the sword, seeming to reminisce about that bygone tale.
The Laureate need not draw his blade any longer, for the Champion shall always strike with his all.

en: Lin Xiansheng once held a hundred-day banquet at the Debating Hall, extending invitations far and wide to men of letters throughout the realm to sit and discourse upon the Way. Over those hundred days, he crossed wits with all challengers and emerged foremost among them. Every last guest who attended conceded defeat and, by common accord, proclaimed the Inkbound Order the sovereign head of the literary world. From that time on, no scholar of any renown who set brush to pages would fail to present their work to the Inkbound Order, each hoping to see it committed to print, and counting such recognition the crowning glory of their life's work.

zh: 舞狮兄弟是达安郑氏暴乱中的幸存者。那年常喜十七岁，常乐六岁。两兄弟眼见宅中血流成河，而亲友尽数亡于流寇刀下。他们第一次知道，原来世道面前，善是如此虚妄与无力。后绝望的常喜抱着昏迷的弟弟仓皇出逃，却因力竭跌入河中，最后是鬼街六煞坤幺儿行经此地，一时心善救下了他们。次日醒来，常乐忘记了发生的一切。常喜便再不提及往事。他深知世道之恶，他无力抗衡；而血仇之深，眼下亦无力得报。于是他默默咽下一切，成为坤幺儿手下舞狮兄弟团的一员，借巡游之名为恩人搜集情报，并暗中等待一个合适的时机。总有一日，他要向这世间的恶，讨回失去的一切。即便代价是，他也会沦为恶的一员。
en: The Twin Lions are survivors of the Da'an Zheng Clan Rebellion. Back then, Chang Xi was seventeen years old, and Chang Le was just six. The two brothers watched helplessly as their home turned into a river of blood, their kin and friends all slaughtered by marauding bandits. It was then they first realized that in this chaotic world, kindness was but a hollow, powerless thing. In despair, Chang Xi fled with his unconscious younger brother in his arms, only to collapse from exhaustion and fall into a river. Kun the Youngest, one of the Six Fiends of Ghost Street, happened to be there and, moved by a rare moment of pity, saved their lives. When Chang Le awoke the next day, he remembered nothing of the horrors they had endured. Chang Xi never spoke of it again. He knew too well the cruelty of the world, a cruelty he could not hope to defy. And he knew the depth of his blood debt, a debt he had no power yet to repay. So, he swallowed his grief and rage, and became a member of the Twin Lions under Kun the Youngest, performing across the land under the guise of festival tours while secretly gathering intelligence for his benefactor. All the while, he waited. Biding his time for the right moment. He vowed that one day he would demand back all that was taken from him. Even if, in doing so, he had to become part of the evil he despised.

zh:
贺然此生离王清最近的时候，是他们的见面那天，一群走投无路的乞儿撞上一位将军的列队和高头大马。
那群乞儿那时候看起来还无般一二，最大的差别不过是你比我高上半个头，他又比我今日多吃了几口馒头，江晏只不过是其中脾气不好的一个，还比其他人矮些。
江晏抱着那把木剑站出列的时候，看起来莽撞，傲气，是这个世道最不容易活下去的那种人，但那位骑在高头大马上的将军却如此喜爱他。

后来的许多年月，贺然把江晏的那几句话翻来覆去地嚼着，无数次在梦中，他回到了那一天，说出那些话，再往前走一步，做那个站出列的人，这样，他就可以拿走江晏的命运，对吗？
他就会成为那个站在将军身边的人，如果是这样，他决不会像江晏一样在院子里追猫，弄得一身脏兮兮；他会做最听将军话的孩子，他会好好习武；他不会贪酒，不会招惹是非，不会让将军日日面对旁人的状告皱眉，却又无可奈何；他会做得比江晏更好。

在梦里，他仰起头，看见了将军的笑，似乎在喊他的名字，他下意识地笑起来，想要张口——
屋檐上的雨水下坠，他的梦被惊醒，他靠在破庙的墙壁上，地面的水渍倒映出一张沾着血迹的脸。
他握着手中的长剑，那把长剑今日刚刚斩下了一颗头颅，装着人头的麻袋滚在他的脚边，他恍恍惚惚地看向周围，对了，是害死将军的人之一，他盯着剑上那抹未干的血迹，他想起来了。
他的将军，三日前死了。

他拄着剑，一步一步向外走去，破庙之外，是天上的雨。
破庙之内，一滴又一滴雨水无声砸落，带着微红的血迹，人的眼泪是地上的雨。
他知道命运不会因为梦境改变。
只是他不明白，为何天上阴雨，甚至不许他将一场完整的梦留下。
en:
The closest He Ran ever came to General Wang Qing was the day they met. A group of beggar kids stumbled into the path of a general's procession, horses tall and gleaming.
 Back then, they were all more or less the same. One might be half a head taller, another had a few extra bites of steamed bun. Jiang Yan was just one of them, a hot-tempered boy, maybe a bit shorter than the rest.
 But when Jiang Yan stepped forward, clutching his wooden sword, brash and proud, he seemed the sort least likely to survive in this world. Yet the general, seated high on his horse, favored him.

 Years later, He Ran would chew on Jiang Yan's words over and over again. In dreams, he returned to that day. But this time, he was the one who stepped forward, said those words, stood before the crowd. This way, he would've become the boy chosen by the general, instead of Jiang Yan, wouldn't he?
 He would've stood at the general's side. And unlike Jiang Yan, he wouldn't chase cats around the courtyard and come back filthy. He'd be the obedient one. He wouldn't drink. Wouldn't cause trouble. Wouldn't leave the general frowning at constant complaints, helpless to defend him. He would've done much better than Jiang Yan. He knew it.

 In the dream, he looked up, and the general was smiling at him, calling his name. He smiled back, instinctively, about to answer...
 Rain fell from the eaves, and the dream shattered. He woke up, leaning against the wall of a ruined temple. The puddle on the ground mirrored a blood-smeared face.
 A long sword in his grip, one that cut off a head today. A gunny sack by his feet, with that head in it. He stared blankly at the drying blood on the blade. Yes... it was one of the men who killed the general. He remembered now.
 Three days ago, his general had died.

 He leaned on his sword and stepped outside. The rain was still falling.
 Inside the ruined temple, rain dripped silently from the roof. Each bead of red-streaked water splashing against the floor like tears from the earth.
 He knew dreams couldn't change fate.
 He just didn't understand why even the sky, full of rain, refused to let him keep a single dream whole.
Dare to run... dare to run...

en:
Your servant, Minister of War Li Tao, respectfully submits: The corvée laborers from Chenliu have fled. Yin Xun actually resorted to extreme torture, cruel and oppressive to the people. Hearing this shocks and angers me.
Although I am ill at home, having long served in the Ministry of War, I know that if a military officer kills an innocent person, how can it be overlooked! The laborers were weary from their service and escaped occasionally. This is not a major crime of treason. Yin Xun arrogantly used heavy punishment, violating the Emperor's benevolent rule and wounding the hearts of the people! Moreover, the Emperor has decreed that after a prefecture decides on a death penalty, the case must be recorded and reported to the Ministry of Justice for review. Yin Xun truly acted against orders!
I beg the Emperor to order Yin Xun beheaded in the market to uphold justice, console the people, and bring peace to the officials and commoners! I bow my head and await the Emperor's decision.

打尔之头，教尔朝梁暮唐不惜名。

en:
30th Day of the First Month, fourth year of Tongguang
A rare day of leisure. I spoke with Master Feng on matters of the Dao and gained much from it, enough to count him a friend.
Then I heard that the times were about to change, and that he meant to cast aside his good name and enter Luoyang. I tried to dissuade him.
1st Day of the Second Month, fourth year of Tongguang
Could not dissuade him. Tried reasoning with him instead.
...
2nd Day of the Second Month, fourth year of Tongguang
Reasoning failed, so I debated him.
...
3rd Day of the Second Month, fourth year of Tongguang
Debate failed. So I laid out the matter in terms of gain and loss.
...

4th Day of the Second Month, fourth year of Tongguang
Gain and loss made no difference. So I tried to appeal to his emotions.
...

5th Day of the Second Month, fourth year of Tongguang
Emotions made no difference. So I wrote and scolded him.
...

6th Day of the Second Month, fourth year of Tongguang
That blasted fellow...
Mind your words, mind your words. How can a gentleman speak to a friend like some petty wretch? I shall try again...

7th Day of the Second Month, fourth year of Tongguang
I have heard that in southern Min there is a method for driving off evil. Today being Jingzhe, I may as well try it and stretch my limbs.
A blow to your head, for making you throw away your good name, chasing Liang at dawn and Tang by dusk.
A blow to your hands, for making you leave behind silk and wealth alike.
A blow to your feet, for making you care for nothing in this world, and seek only the Dao.
A blow to your brow, for making you show bounty to the people, yet no loyalty to your ruler.
A blow to your ears, for making you heed nothing of propriety, righteousness, integrity, or shame.
A blow to your tongue, for making you refuse to speak plainly what your heart knows full well.
A blow to your heart, for all this foolishness, with neither talent nor virtue in it.
...

Ha. This method is excellent. Tomorrow I may argue with that fellow for three hundred more times...
18th Day of the Second Month, fourth year of Tongguang
Though Jingzhe has passed, the method for driving off evil can hardly be called too much.
Strike...
You Hao

zh:
【僖公上第五】

【经】
元年，春，王正月。
○齐师、宋师、曹师次于聂北，救邢。
○夏，六月，邢迁于夷仪。
○齐师、宋师、曹师城邢。
○秋，七月，戊辰，夫人姜氏薨于夷，齐人以归。
○楚人伐郑。
○八月，公会齐侯、宋公、郑伯、曹伯、邾人于柽。
○九月，公败邾师于偃。
○冬，十月，壬午，公子友帅师败莒师于郦，获莒挐。
○十有二月，丁巳，夫人氏之丧至自齐。
【传】
元年，春，不称即位，公出故也。公出复入，不书，讳之也。讳国恶，礼也。
○诸侯救邢。邢人溃，出奔师。师遂逐狄人，具邢器用而迁之，师无私焉。
○夏，邢迁于夷仪。诸侯城之，救患也。凡侯伯，救患、分灾、讨罪，礼也。
○秋，楚人伐郑，郑即齐故也。盟于荦，谋救郑也。
○九月，公败邾师于偃，虚丘之戍将归者也。
○冬，莒人来求赂，公子友败诸郦，获莒子之弟挐。非卿也，嘉获之也。公赐季友汶阳之田及费。
○夫人氏之丧至自齐。君子以齐人之杀哀姜也，为已甚矣。女子，从人者也。

【经】
二年，春，王正月，城楚丘。
○夏，五月，辛巳，葬我小君哀姜。
○虞师、晋师灭下阳。
○秋，九月，齐侯、宋公、江人、黄人盟于贯。
○冬，十月，不雨。
○楚人侵郑。
【传】
二年，春，诸侯城楚丘而封卫焉。不书所会，后也。
○晋荀息请以屈产之乘与垂棘之璧，假道于虞以伐虢。公曰：“是吾宝也。”对曰：“若得道于虞，犹外府也。”公曰：“宫之奇存焉。”对曰：“宫之奇之为人也，懦而不能强谏，且少长于君，君昵之，虽谏，将不听。”乃使荀息假道于虞，曰：“冀为不道，入自颠𫐉，伐鄍三门。冀之既病，则亦唯君故。今虢为不道，保于逆旅，以侵敝邑之南鄙。敢请假道以请罪于虢。”虞公许之，且请先伐虢。宫之奇谏，不听，遂起师。夏，晋里克、荀息帅师会虞师伐虢，灭下阳。先书虞，贿故也。
○秋，盟于贯，服江、黄也。
○齐寺人貂始漏师于多鱼。
○虢公败戎于桑田。晋卜偃曰：“虢必亡矣。亡下阳不惧，而又有功，是天夺之鉴，而益其疾也。必易晋而不抚其民矣，不可以五稔。”
○冬，楚人伐郑。斗章囚郑聃伯。
……
en:
[Book 5, Duke Xi, Part I]

[The Classic]
It was the duke's first year, the spring, the king's first month.
An army of Qi, an army of Song, and an army of Cao halted at Niebei, in proceeding to the rescue of Xing.
In summer, in the sixth month, Xing removed its capital to Yiyi.
The army of Qi, an army of Song, and an army of Cao walled the new capital of Xing.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on Wuchen, duke Zhuang's wife, the lady Jiang, died at Yi, an officer of Qi taking her body back with him.
A body of men from Chu invaded Zheng.
In the eighth month, the duke had a meeting with the marquis of Qi, the duke of Song, the earl of Zheng, the earl of Cao, and an officer of Zhu, in Cheng.
In the ninth month, the duke defeated an army of Zhu at Yan.
In winter, in the tenth month, on Renwu, duke Huan's son You led an army and defeated an army of Ju at Li, taking Na of Ju.
In the twelfth month, on Dingsi, the coffin of duke Zhuang's wife arrived from Qi.

[The Classic]
In the duke's second year, in spring, in the king's first month, we aided in the walling of Chuqiu.
In summer, in the fifth month, on Xinsi, we buried our duchess, Ai Jiang.
An army of Yu and an army of Jin extinguished Xiayang.
In autumn, in the ninth month, the marquis of Qi, the duke of Song, an officer of Jiang, and an officer of Huang, made a covenant in Guan.
In winter, in the tenth month, there was no rain.
A body of men from Chu made an incursion into Zheng.

zh:
晋王李克用翻覆如云，前脚遣用，后脚伪托他将之名追杀，高思继便是被那过河拆桥的刀锋逼入绝境。
可晋王身畔那蒙面谋士，暗中遣死士递来口信，教高思继险险脱了一劫。死士携一布包前来，将谋士之言一字不漏传到：“君赤诚报国，锐意无歇，此身不当死于此处。”
然高思继连战数阵，枪折马疲，已是强弩之末。四顾茫然，主君相弃，天地虽阔，竟无他容身之地。
他解开布包，内里是数张细描的舆图，皆标着守备薄弱之处，另有一枚酒葫芦。
高思继好饮，从前与那谋士对坐闲谈时曾放言：“若得好酒足醉，千军万马也拦不住我高思继。”
那书生竟当真了么？单凭这一葫芦薄酿，便想教他凭身而免，直抵那飞鸟不至的自在之处？
他拔塞仰首，一饮而尽。
酒入喉肠，既有人信他如此，他又怎好教人空付一场期许？便以拳为武，依醉为凭，看阵！

“那曾祖到底逃没逃出来啊？”
时一墨受不了她爹把故事断在这，缠着叫他讲完。
时九歌看看墙上挂着的属于横剑山庄家传的葫芦，起身给幼女铺被。
“小祖宗，今日就到这吧！你若乖乖随你娘亲睡下，明日便给你讲。”
en:
Li Keyong, the Prince of Jin, was as unpredictable as the shifting clouds. He would put Gao Siji to use one moment, only to send assassins under another general's banner to hunt him down the next. Gao Siji was driven to the absolute brink by this ruthless betrayal.
However, a masked advisor in the Prince's inner circle secretly sent an agent with a message, helping Gao narrowly escape his doom. The agent brought a cloth bundle and relayed the advisor's words verbatim: "Your loyalty to the realm is pure, and your spirit unbroken. You are not meant to die here."
But after surviving wave after wave of ambushes, Gao Siji was entirely spent, his spear shattered, his horse driven to exhaustion. Looking around in despair, abandoned by his lord, he realized that despite the vastness of the world, there was nowhere left for him to hide.
He opened the bundle. Inside were several meticulously drawn maps highlighting the weak points in the enemy's blockade, along with a single wine gourd.
Gao Siji was a man who loved his wine. Once, while sharing a drink with that very advisor, he had boldly boasted: "Give me enough good wine to get properly drunk, and an army of thousands couldn't stop me!"
Did the scholar actually take him seriously? Did he really expect him to survive with nothing but his bare hands, fueled by nothing but a gourd of cheap brew, and fight his way to total freedom?
Gao pulled the stopper, threw his head back, and drained it in a single gulp.
As the wine burned down his throat, a thought struck him: If there is still someone in this world who believes in me this much, how can I let them down? With only his bare fists for weapons and the wine's fire for strength, he roared: "Watch me break your lines!"

"So did Great-Grandpa actually get away or what?!"
Shi Yimo couldn't stand it when her father left stories on a cliffhanger, begging him to finish the tale.
Shi Jiuge glanced up at the old gourd hanging on the wall, a treasured heirloom of Crossblade Manor, and stood up to tuck his little girl into bed.
"Alright, you little troublemaker, that's enough for today! If you're a good girl and go to sleep for your mother, I'll tell you the rest tomorrow."

A sharpener would constantly adjust his grinding angle to match the specific tool, and his ultimate test of quality was whether the newly sharpened blade could effortlessly slice through a piece of fabric. 起风了。风车醒了。叶片哗啦啦地旋开，像一朵绽放的花。而$T(30)透过那飞旋的彩光望出去——天空被染上胭脂，游弋的鱼灯曳出金线，连远处模糊的吆喝声，都仿佛化作了流动的光斑。
一个很大、很慢、温柔得不像话的世界……就在$T(30)的眼前。
en:
A child got separated from the group in the middle of the lantern fair.
But $T(30) did not cry, and did not go running around looking for anyone either. After making one loop through the crowd, $T(30) found an old wooden crate for storing lanterns and sat down on it.
An old man selling sugar figurines spotted the child from a distance. He slowly made his way over and handed over a paper pinwheel he had just finished.
"Don't worry," he said, his voice soft and slow. "The person looking for you is already on the way."
The child nodded. And truly, $T(30) was not afraid.
Then the wind picked up. The pinwheel began to turn. Its blades opened in a rush, like a flower coming into bloom. Through that spinning burst of color, $T(30) looked out and saw the whole fair transformed—the sky was flushed pink, fish lanterns drifted by trailing lines of gold, and even the distant cries from the street seemed to blur into the lights.
For a moment, the whole world in front of the child felt huge, slow, and softer than it had any right to be.

zh:
小铸剑室里坐了位大将军。
这是我第三次为破白烧炉子。将军，你拿它打了多少场仗，取了多少人头？
将军摇摇头，不记得了。
它吃了很多人。吃到白的地方能看到发黑的痕迹，黑的地方露出了灰白的瘢痕。不过，这是剑，剑就是这么用的。
我把烧红的剑身放到砧子上，铸剑室里总算是有了点声音。一锤抚平百姓眉，一锤砸碎敌人骨。飞溅的火花里，将军望着他的老伙计，眼神如同十七岁的他一样清冽。
你做了将军，想要什么神兵利刃，都有人争相给你送来。你为何要花大价钱、大力气补破白？
它在我手中一日，便是世间最好的剑。你尚在这世间一日，便是破白最后的底气。我要用破白，杀敌，收土，踏遍河西。
我用力往破白身上敲去。破白啊破白，一个铸剑的听不懂他说什么，你应当听得懂吧？
将军拿了破白，漏夜离开。末了，嘱咐我长长久久地活着，等着他把黎明带到河西的那天。
en:
A great general sat in my small forging room. 
This was the third time I'd heated the furnace for Palebreak. "General, how many battles have you fought with it? How many lives has it claimed?" 
The general shook his head. "I don't remember." 
It has 'eaten' many people. The white parts are stained black, the black parts show gray scars. But this is a sword, that's what swords are for. 
I placed the red-hot blade on the anvil, finally filling the forging room with sound. One hammer strike to smooth the wrinkles on the people's brows, one strike to shatter the enemies' bones. Amidst the flying sparks, the general looked at his old companion, his eyes as clear as they were when he was seventeen. 
Now that you're a general, people scramble to offer you divine weapons. Why spend so much money and effort repairing Palebreak? 
As long as it's in my hand, it's the best sword in the world. As long as you're alive, Palebreak has its final courage. I will use Palebreak to kill enemies, reclaim land, and traverse Hexi. 
I struck Palebreak hard. "Palebreak, Palebreak, I'm just a swordsmith, I don't understand his words. But you must, right?" 
The general took Palebreak and left at night. Before he left, he told me to live a long life, wait for the day he brings dawn to Hexi.

zh:
河边总会长出一片芦苇草。
无人播种，也无人照料。春时青青，秋时苍苍。
当风吹过，整片芦苇簌簌作响，一齐朝着一个方向弯下了腰。

常在河边生活的人都知道，芦草能做许多东西。
铺在屋顶上，能挡风遮雨；垫在粮车板上，能少些颠簸；编成席子，多少能保温取暖；就算是空心的芦管，也能拿来吹些不成调的曲子……

许多年以后，也许会有人站在河边指点：
“话说当年，将军在此力战。”
“又说当年，某侠在此断敌。”
但很少有人会问，那些河边的芦苇草做了什么呢？
也许，是塞在那几辆赶赴前线的粮车里，当作一层草垫，被血水和雨水一块浸透；
也许，是被扔进战地的火堆里，烧得劈啪作响，只换来几只冻僵的手指能再握一握刀；
也许，它们什么也没做，只是站在河岸，默默看着，倔强站着，不肯被风吹弯下腰。

后来，又有几根芦草被人割下。
它被削薄、晾干，裁出手臂、肩背，又被涂上颜色，扎上细线。
戏台点灯，白幕亮起，台前的才子佳人，帝王将相又轮番登台。
而那道芦草的影子就在幕布上无人在意的角落里，沉默地站着。

台下的孩子仰着头，问身旁的人：
“那个影子是谁呀？”
“那个啊，没名字的人。”
孩子想了想，指着那影子说：
“太好了，那就是我！我的名字，给它。”

灯火颤了颤，影子点了点头。
en:
Reeds always grow by the river. No one sows them, and no one tends them. They are green in spring and gray in autumn. When the wind blows, the entire field rustles, bowing together in one direction.

Those who live by the river know that reeds can be made into many things. They cover roofs to keep out the wind and rain; they pad grain carts to soften the jolts; they are woven into mats for warmth. Even a hollow reed can be used to whistle a tuneless song...

Many years later, someone might stand by the river and point:
"They say the general fought a great battle here."
"And they say a certain hero cut down the enemy here."

But few will ask: what did the reeds by the river do?

Perhaps they were stuffed into grain carts bound for the front lines, serving as a layer of padding, soaked through with blood and rain.
Perhaps they were tossed into a battlefield fire, crackling as they burned, just so a few frozen fingers could grip a blade once more.
Or perhaps they did nothing at all, simply standing on the bank, watching in silence, stubbornly refusing to let the wind bow their heads.

Later, a few more reeds were cut down. They were thinned, dried, and shaped into arms and backs, then painted and tied with fine string.

The stage lights up, the white screen glows, and the scholars, beauties, emperors, and generals take their turns on stage. But the shadow of the reed stands in a corner where no one notices, silent.

A child below the stage looks up and asks:
"Who is that shadow?"
"That? The nameless one."

The child thinks for a moment, points at the shadow, and says:
"Perfect, that's me! I will give it my name."

The lamplight flickers, and the shadow nods.

zh:
【隐公第一】

元年，春，王正月。
元年者何？君之始年也。春者何？岁之始也。王者孰谓？谓文王也。曷为先言王而后言正月？王正月也。何言乎王正月？大一统也。公何以不言即位？成公意也。何成乎公之意？公将平国而反之桓。曷为反之桓？桓幼而贵，隐长而卑。其为尊卑也微，国人莫知。隐长又贤，诸大夫扳隐而立之。隐于是焉而辞立，则未知桓之将必得立也。且如桓立，则恐诸大夫之不能相幼君也，故凡隐之立，为桓立也。隐长又贤，何以不宜立？立适以长不以贤，立子以贵不以长。桓何以贵？母贵也。母贵，则子何以贵？子以母贵，母以子贵。
〇三月，公及邾娄仪父盟于眛。
及者何？与也。会、及、暨，皆与也，曷为或言会，或言及，或言暨？会，犹最也；及，犹汲汲也；暨，犹暨暨也。及，我欲之；暨，不得已也。仪父者何？邾娄之君也。何以名？字也。曷为称字？褒之也。曷为褒之？为其与公盟也。与公盟者众矣，曷为独褒乎此？因其可褒而褒之。此其为可褒奈何？渐进也。昧者何？地期也。
〇夏，五月，郑伯克段于鄢。
克之者何？杀之也。杀之则曷为谓之克？大郑伯之恶也。曷为大郑伯之恶？母欲立之，己杀之，如勿与而已矣。段者何？郑伯之弟也。何以不称弟？当国也。其地何？当国也。齐人杀无知，何以不地？在内也。在内，虽当国，不地也；不当国，虽在外，亦不地也。
〇秋，七月，天王使宰咺来归惠公、仲子之赗。
宰者何？官也。咺者何？名也。曷为以官氏？宰，士也。惠公者何？隐之考也。仲子者何？桓之母也。何以不称夫人？桓未君也。赗者何？丧事有赗。赗者，盖以马，以乘马束帛。车马曰赗，货财曰赙，衣被曰禭。桓未君，则诸侯曷为来赗之？隐为桓立，故以桓母之丧告于诸侯。然则何言尔？成公意也。其言来何？不及事也。其言惠公、仲子何？兼之。兼之，非礼也。何以不言及仲子？仲子微也。
〇九月，及宋人盟于宿。
孰及之？内之微者也。
〇冬，十有二月，祭伯来。
祭伯者何？天子之大夫也。何以不称使？奔也。奔则曷为不言奔？王者无外，言奔，则有外之辞也。
〇公子益师卒。
何以不日？远也。所见异辞，所闻异辞，所传闻异辞。
……
en:
【Duke Yin, First Year】

First Year, Spring, the King's First Month.
What does "First Year" mean? It is the first year of a ruler's reign. What does "Spring" mean? It is the beginning of the year. Who is referred to as "the King"? It refers to King Wen. Why does it say "King" before "First Month"? Because it is the King's First Month. Why mention the King's First Month? To emphasize the great unity under one rule. Why does the Duke not announce his accession? To fulfill the Duke's intention. What is the Duke's intention? The Duke intended to pacify the state and then return it to Duke Huan. Why return it to Duke Huan? Because Duke Huan was young but of noble birth, while Duke Yin was older but of lower status. The difference in their status was subtle, and the people of the state did not know of it. Duke Yin was older and virtuous, and the various high officials supported Duke Yin to establish him as ruler. If Duke Yin had declined the position at that time, it was uncertain whether Duke Huan would surely be established. Moreover, if Duke Huan were established, Duke Yin feared that the officials might not be able to assist the young ruler. Therefore, Duke Yin's accession was for the sake of Duke Huan's eventual accession. Since Duke Yin was older and virtuous, why was it not appropriate for him to be established? In establishing the rightful heir, one chooses by seniority, not by virtue; in establishing a son, one chooses by nobility of birth, not by seniority. Why was Duke Huan noble? Because his mother was noble. If the mother is noble, then why is the son noble? The son is noble because of the mother, and the mother is noble because of the son.
〇Third Month, the Duke met with Yifu of Zhulou at Mei.
What does "met with" mean? It means to associate with. "Meeting," "associating," and "joining" all mean to associate, but why sometimes say "meeting," sometimes "associating," and sometimes "joining"? "Meeting" is like gathering together; "associating" implies eagerness; "joining" implies reluctance. "Associating" means it was our desire; "joining" means it was unavoidable. Who is Yifu? He is the ruler of Zhulou. Why is he named? It is his courtesy name. Why use his courtesy name? To praise him. Why praise him? Because he formed an alliance with the Duke. Many formed alliances with the Duke; why is he alone praised here? Because he is praiseworthy, and so he is praised. In what way is he praiseworthy? He gradually advanced toward proper conduct. What is Mei? It is the place of the meeting.
〇Summer, Fifth Month, the Earl of Zheng overcame Duan at Yan.
What does "overcame" mean? It means to kill him. If he killed him, then why call it "overcame"? To magnify the wickedness of the Earl of Zheng. Why magnify the Earl of Zheng's wickedness? His mother wanted to establish Duan, but he killed him—it would have been better not to have given him anything at all. Who is Duan? He is the younger brother of the Earl of Zheng. Why is he not called "younger brother"? Because he acted as if he were the ruler of the state. Why is the place mentioned? Because he acted as if he were the ruler of the state. When the people of Qi killed Wuzhi, why is the place not mentioned? Because it was within their own borders. If within their own borders, even if the person acted as ruler, the place is not mentioned; if not acting as ruler, even if outside their borders, the place is also not mentioned.
〇Autumn, Seventh Month, the Heavenly King sent the steward Xuan to present funeral gifts for Duke Hui and Zhongzi.
What is "steward"? It is an office. What is "Xuan"? It is a name. Why use the office as a surname? Because the steward is a minor officer. Who is Duke Hui? He is the late father of Duke Yin. Who is Zhongzi? She is the mother of Duke Huan. Why is she not called "Lady"? Because Duke Huan was not yet ruler. What are funeral gifts? In mourning rites, there are funeral gifts. Funeral gifts consist of horses, and also of teams of horses and bolts of silk. Chariots and horses are called "fèng," goods and wealth are called "fù," and clothing and coverings are called "suì." Since Duke Huan was not yet ruler, why did the feudal lords come to present funeral gifts? Because Duke Yin was established for Duke Huan's sake, he therefore announced the mourning for Duke Huan's mother to the feudal lords. Then why say this? To fulfill the Duke's intention. Why say "came"? Because it was after the funeral had already taken place. Why mention both Duke Hui and Zhongzi? Because they were combined. Combining them is not according to ritual. Why not say "and Zhongzi"? Because Zhongzi was of low status.
〇Ninth Month, [Our state] made an alliance with the people of Song at Su.
Who made the alliance? A minor person from within our state.
〇Winter, Twelfth Month, Caibo came.
Who is Caibo? He is a high official of the Heavenly King. Why is it not said that he was sent? Because he was fleeing. If he was fleeing, then why not say "fleeing"? Because the King has no outside; saying "fleeing" would imply that there is an outside.
〇Gongzi Yishi died.
Why is the day not recorded? Because it was in the distant past. What one sees is spoken of differently, what one hears is spoken of differently, and what one hears by transmission is spoken of differently.
……

zh:
若无所明。则无明觉。有所非觉。无所非明。无明又非……

无同……呵呵，我付出了一切，只为守城……

en:
If there is nothing to perceive, there is no clear awareness. Awareness arises only in relation to an object; without one, even ignorance cannot be treated as something known.
Awareness itself does not depend on what is perceived. The very impulse to know creates the illusion of an object, and from this illusion come imaginary distinctions. In our original state, there is no "same" or "different."
No "same"... Heh... I gave my all just to protect the city...
But now... the city's fallen too...
No... it can't end like this...
No... no... no...

zh:
年轻人：
       好久不见，最近过得还好吗？
       托你的福，摊子的生意很好。你阿婶她很久没有这么高兴了，每天笑盈盈地和来往客人唠家常，开心的时候还会借着琵琶摊小娘子的曲子跳上几步！不忙的时候，老张和老幺还张罗着去和赛神队的几个小伙子比赛，哈哈。
      天水集的大伙儿都会提起你，说你行侠仗义，我们听着都很开心，也惦记着你。你阿婶怕你在外面吃不饱穿不暖，时常念叨你呢。有时间就来摊子坐坐啊。
      对了，开烫菜摊子赚了些钱，我们想着也帮衬帮衬别人，就做了些饭菜送给了几个老伙计。怕他们觉得不好意思，我们几个就说，是你要给他们送的。他们还奇怪，说怎么会有没见过的好心人惦记他们呢。老张说这孩子就是这样的，是个热心肠的大侠！他们不太好意思，就给你写了字条，你一起看看吧。
      好了，不说了，待会要来客人了，就到这儿吧。
      希望你一个人在外吃饱穿暖，平平安安。
<IMAGE id='im1' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/6891d8bdfe8439c141990d35dFy5PtiF06' size='2290*1296' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>
en:
Young Hero: 
Long time no see. How have you been? 
Thanks to you, the stall is doing great. Your Auntie hasn't been this happy in ages—she smiles, chatting with customers all day, and even dances a few steps when the Pipa lady plays! When it's slow, Old Zhang and Old Yao even try to race the lads from the deity competition team, haha. 
Everyone at Skybrim Market speaks of your chivalry. We are happy to hear it and miss you often. Your Auntie worries you aren't eating well or staying warm. She talks about you all the time. Come visit the stall when you can. 
Oh, we made some money from the scalding vegetable stall, so we thought we'd help others out. We sent some food to a few old partners. We were afraid they'd feel embarrassed, so we said it was from you. They were surprised a kind hero remembered them! Old Zhang said, "That child is just warm-hearted like that!" They were shy, so they wrote you notes. Take a look. 
Okay, customers are coming. I'll stop here. 
Stay warm, fed, and safe out there.

zh:
昔墨山道建飞天城，欲上贯云霓，衍算天机，以济苍生。未料宏愿未酬，城郭先颓，倏忽三载矣。
今残垣之内，异声渐次，机巧之声，律若心搏。又见虫兽翔集，鸣声各异，青鸟掠影，盘桓故墟，诸猴痴妄，望水捞月。夫水中之影，天上月耶？缥缈梦耶？
后之来者，或可于波澜间，探水中月之真假，飞天梦之虚实。
en:
Long ago, Mohist Hill built the Skyward City, hoping to pierce the clouds, unlock Heaven's secrets, and bring relief to the common people. Yet before that great ambition could be fulfilled, the city fell to ruin. Three years have passed in the blink of an eye.
Now, within the broken walls, strange sounds stir once more. The whir of mechanisms beats like a heart. Insects and beasts gather in flight, each with its own cry. Azure birds flash past and circle the old ruins. The monkeys, lost in folly, try to scoop the moon from the water. But is the moon in the water truly the moon above, or only a passing dream?
Those who come after may yet search the rippling water for the truth behind the moon's reflection, and learn whether Skyward City's dream was real or merely an illusion.

To the Esteemed Youxia-er:

As winter chills, we send our regards.

After several seasons, "Yanyun Sixteen Tones" finally meets you all. Thanks to your trust, Yanyun has welcomed #Y3 million wanderers#E. The once #Ygreenhorn#E now presents their answer sheet—though "passing" isn't the end of Yanyun's tale. We'll always remember: never abandon ideals against the wind, and keep improving under scrutiny.

We're even more grateful to walk this path with you, shaping Yanyun's story together. It's you and "Yanyun Sixteen Tones" who've built today's Jianghu. Deeply moved, we dare not forget.

All of Sixteen Lanes hereby offer a #4d734dtoken of gratitude#E. Let this also be a pledge: on the long road ahead, urge us to honor the #Ygreenhorn's vow#E—hold true to our初心, fear no path, train hard, for martial arts know no bounds!

May we share Jianghu's splendor, ride side by side through endless lands.

卷卷是宋若卿的小狗，最爱蜷在她的官靴旁晒太阳。
旁人眼里的宋若卿冷面无情，总把宫女训得掉眼泪。可她们不知道，这位严厉的女官会在四下无人时，把卷卷搂进怀里，握着它暖乎乎的爪子喃喃自语：“我是不是太严厉了？她们还只是群孩子……”
别人总想教卷卷学规矩，学坐下、学禁声，唯独宋若卿只希望它无忧无虑，顿顿饱饭。卷卷似懂非懂，也许“规矩”是人世间很重要的东西，可有什么比热乎乎的饭更重要呢？日子很长，肚子饱饱的，一切才有盼头。
en:
Curly is Song Ruoqing's little dog. It loves nothing more than curling up in the sun beside her official boots.



To others, Song Ruoqing seems stern and unapproachable, often scolding maids until they cry. What they don't see is that when no one is around, she pulls Curly into her arms, holds its warm paws, and murmurs to herself, "Am I being too harsh? They're still just children..."



People try to teach Curly "rules", to sit on command, to stay quiet. Song Ruoqing is the only one who simply wants it to be carefree, with a full bowl at every meal.



Curly half understands. Maybe "rules" matter in the human world. But what could matter more than a hot meal? The days are long, and with a full belly, there is always something to hope for.

胜者洋洋得意，败者也不垂头丧气。围观的稚童们更是争先恐后地重来一盘。
杜不弈很擅长嫖姚棋。每次起手，他都会想象自己就是个大将军。
挥斥方遒，锐不可挡。或许也正是这样的信念在，杜不弈的棋总能接二连三得手。
他为自己的连胜而骄傲。
可令他哭笑不得的是，最终，他会被一串葡萄打败。
en:
Du Buyi had been a chess prodigy since childhood. 
Piaoyao Battleboard was very popular among children in Hexi. Three or five mischievous kids could get together for a match. 
The winner would be smug, the loser wouldn't be dejected. The watching children would clamor for another round. 
Du Buyi excelled at playing Piaoyao Battleboard. Every time he made a move, he would imagine himself as a great general. 
Commanding with ease, irresistibly sharp. Perhaps it was precisely this conviction that allowed Du Buyi's pieces to connect and win repeatedly.
He was proud of his winning streak. 
But ironically, he would ultimately be defeated by a bunch of grapes.

常见的本土鹦鹉特征为翠羽赤喙。宋代罗愿《尔雅翼·释鸟》记载：“鹦鹉，能言之鸟，其状似鸮，绿羽赤啄足，陇右及南中皆有之。”故鹦鹉又名为陇客。
en:
Parrots have appeared as decorative motifs as early as the Shang dynasty. Across later dynasties, they were prized as ornamental birds and widely kept in both palaces and private homes.
Native parrots were commonly described as having emerald-green plumage and red beaks. Luo Yuan writes in Erya Yi (Wings to the Erya), "The parrot is a bird that can speak. It resembles an owl in shape, with green feathers, a red beak and feet. It is found in Longyou and in Nanzhong."
For this reason, the parrot was also known by the byname "Longyou Guest."

zh:
又是一年春节了。医馆里也热热闹闹的，但这里热闹确是因为往来的病人。
病了的孩子吃了药一时还没好，疼得眼泪直掉，说自己想吃桂花糕。
药药看了眼泪汪汪的孩子，出门向点心摊去。
孩子不哭了。或许是因为药发挥作用了，又或许是因为嘴里那块桂花糕。
夜更深了，病人们陆续离开，医馆终于安静了。
忙碌的药药得空坐下了。
桂花糕好香啊，药药想。
新的一年，她要奖励自己一块桂花糕。
en:
Another Spring Festival has arrived. The clinic is bustling with the steady stream of patients coming in.
A sick child hasn't recovered though they've taken medication, and has tears streaming down from the pain, saying they want some osmanthus cake.
Yaoyao saw the state of the tearful child and headed out toward the pastry stall.
The child stopped crying. Perhaps the medicine had taken effect, or perhaps it was the osmanthus cake in their mouth.
The sky gets darker with night. The patients leave one by one, and the clinic finally grows quiet.
The busy Yaoyao finally has a moment to sit down.
The osmanthus cake smells so good, Yaoyao thought.
To celebrate the new year, she will treat herself to a piece of osmanthus cake.

zh:
年轻人：
       好久不见，最近过得还好吗？
       托你的福，摊子的生意很好。你阿婶她很久没有这么高兴了，每天笑盈盈地和来往客人唠家常，开心的时候还会借着琵琶摊小娘子的曲子跳上几步！不忙的时候，老张和老幺还张罗着去和赛神队的几个小伙子比赛，哈哈。
      天水集的大伙儿都会提起你，说你行侠仗义，我们听着都很开心，也惦记着你。你阿婶怕你在外面吃不饱穿不暖，时常念叨你呢。有时间就来摊子坐坐啊。
      对了，开烫菜摊子赚了些钱，我们想着也帮衬帮衬别人，就做了些饭菜送给了几个老伙计。怕他们觉得不好意思，我们几个就说，是你要给他们送的。他们还奇怪，说怎么会有没见过的好心人惦记他们呢。老张说这孩子就是这样的，是个热心肠的大侠！他们不太好意思，就给你写了字条，你一起看看吧。
      好了，不说了，待会要来客人了，就到这儿吧。
      希望你一个人在外吃饱穿暖，平平安安。
<IMAGE id='im1' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/6891d88cf63d180f7ee0d4f4OSH69uvo06' size='2290*1296' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>
en:
Young Hero: 
Long time no see. How have you been? 
Thanks to you, the stall is doing great. Your Auntie hasn't been this happy in ages—she smiles, chatting with customers all day, and even dances a few steps when the Pipa lady plays! When it's slow, Old Zhang and Old Yao even try to race the lads from the deity competition team, haha. 
Everyone at Skybrim Market speaks of your chivalry. We are happy to hear it and miss you often. Your Auntie worries you aren't eating well or staying warm. She talks about you all the time. Come visit the stall when you can. 
Oh, we made some money from the scalding vegetable stall, so we thought we'd help others out. We sent some food to a few old partners. We were afraid they'd feel embarrassed, so we said it was from you. They were surprised a kind hero remembered them! Old Zhang said, "That child is just warm-hearted like that!" They were shy, so they wrote you notes. Take a look. 
Okay, customers are coming. I'll stop here. 
Stay warm, fed, and safe out there.

可怜九月初三夜，露似真珠月似弓。
en:
[Geography: I]

[Mountain]

In The Mountain
Wang Wei
The white stones gleam in the stream so bright; red leaves fall thin in the cold autumn light.
No rain falls on the winding hill; the green mist wets my gown with its chilly might.

Gazing at the Gate of Heaven Mountain
Li Bai
The river cleaves the heavenly gate in twain; the blue waves eastward flow and turn again.
From either bank green mountains stand in row; a single sail comes from the sun's bright glow.

Gazing at Mount Tai
Du Fu
How magnificent then art thou, Mount Tai? Astride two states green ranges rise sky-high.
Nature in her well-wrought masterpiece took pride; thy light and shade on opposite slopes divide.
The masses of rising vapors broaden my breast, my eyes strained for birds winging to their nest.
Surely will I reach the mountain top some day, and thus watch the hills in miniature lay.

[Village]

Visiting an Old Friend's Farm
Meng Haoran
My friend prepares chicken and millet to share; he invites me to his cottage, a place so fair.
Green trees surround the village, in a close band; blue hills lean beyond the walls, in the far land.
I open the window to face the fields and ground; over wine we talk of mulberry and hemp around.
When the Double Ninth Festival comes to stay; I'll come again to enjoy the chrysanthemums in display.

Farm Homes on the Wei River
Wang Wei
The slanting sun lights the village below; in narrow lanes, flocks and herds go.
The old man minds his herd boy so dear; leaning on staff, he waits by the door near.
The pheasant calls where wheat is tall; silkworms rest on leaves, in a thrall.
The farmer comes with hoe in hand; they chat friendly, on the land.
I admire this leisure and peace; but sigh and chant "Homeward" with ease.

Rain over the Mountain Village
Wang Jian
In rain one or two cocks crow by the cottage door; by bamboo stream and village path, the plank bridge bends lower.
The women call each other to bathe the silkworms so; Idly I watch the gardenias in the courtyard grow.

Village Walk
Du Mu
In mid-spring, west of Nanyang I go; the tender mulberries past the village flow.
The willow branches sway in the breeze so light; the raindrops dot the pond in rings of white.
A cowherd in straw cloak sings his tune; a maid in red peeps through the fence at noon.
Half-damp, I take off my travel coat; the host serves chicken and millet, a hearty note.

[Wilderness]

Gazing at the Wilds
Wang Ji
At dusk I gaze from Eastern Hill, but where can I find my rest?
The trees are all in autumn hue, the hills in sunset dressed.
The herdsman drives his calves back home, the hunter brings his game.
We look at each other, but none I know—I sing of ancient fame.

Wild Walk
Bai Juyi
My robe is heavy with dew on the grass; my clogs are light on the dry sand, as I pass.
I raise my head to hear the bird's song; I stroll along, watching flowers ere long.
On leisure days, no official care I keep; in my declining years, a tranquil mind is deep.
This fleeting life is shorter than a dream; in dreams, do not strive and scheme.

[River]

Boating on the Han River
Wang Wei
The southern fortress meets the three streams' bound; the nine branches from Jingmen flow around.
The river rolls beyond the earth and sky; the mountains' hues are there, yet none descry.
The towns seem floating on the shore so wide; the billows heave the distant sky with pride.
The wind and sun in Xiangyang are so fine; I'd stay and drink with the old hermit divine.

Writing My Thoughts on a Night Journey
Du Fu
The grass blades tremble in the breeze by the shore; a lonely mast stands on the boat at night's core.
The stars bend low across the vast plain wide; the moon swells in the river's rushing tide.
Does fame come from the verses that I write? My post I lost through age and sickness slight.
What am I like, drifting in this world of mine? A lone gull between the earth and sky's design.

Ode to the Evening River
Bai Juyi
The setting sun casts on the water its dye; half green, half red, the river's beauty I spy.
How fair the third night of the ninth moon so high; dew like pearls, moon like a bow in the sky.

天陉绝顶，云海翻腾处，有一浮英野坡，绵延百里，银絮纷飞。由此东去三里，又见摇光天池，每逢秋雨如注，水满洼塘，天合一线。
如此胜地，天地星河尽收眼底，自古以来便催生了诸多传闻。
一说，千年以前，有仙人降落凡尘，于此播撒种子，启蒙明星；
一说，百年以前，有贤人卧湖观天，于此载录星图，传世流芳；
一说，今时今日，有匠人临崖建屋，于此俯仰测绘，著述如山。
……
传说虽不可考，但与星子结缘千年之地，已得赐美名——卧星岩。
en:
At Heaven's Threshold's summit, clouds roll like a sea. There lies a slope named Driftseed Moor, a vast meadow stretching hundreds of miles, covered in drifting silver fluff. Three miles east, Heavenly Pond shimmers.
From here, the heavens and Milky Way unfold in full view, a sight that has inspired legends for centuries.
One says that a thousand years ago, an immortal scattered seeds that awakened enlightenment.
Another tells of a sage who lay by the lake a century past, mapping the stars. The charts are still treasured today.
A more recent tale speaks of artisans who built cliffside dwellings, surveying sky and mountain into voluminous works.
...
Legends may fade unverified, yet this place's thousand-year bond with the stars has earned it a revered name: Stellabed Rocks.

March 13th 
Mom says the "true form of the Evil Shade" has been lost to time and that there's no way it can come back. But I don't believe it! I'm going to find it. 
Xiaoxiao says clan Chief Zhu Zhu's scroll has records of it. I have to check it out tomorrow at the disciples' residence. 

April 10th 
I found the scroll! It really has records of the Evil Shade's true form. But Uncle Ren won't even talk to me... 
He said that I'm not a Nine Mortal Ways disciple, so I can't look at it. Even Grannie Yin wouldn't tell me more...

zh:
“那我们说好了！要一起活下去，要让天下常平，不知饥馑！”
沈义伦第一次听到这句约定的时候，还是个十二三岁的少年。那时的他还不能理解“天下常平”的含义，又或者笑着说出这句话的郑阮也未必明白。可是年少的沈义伦还是本能地对这句话中描述的图景心生向往，再加上跟随郑鄂是他多年养成的习惯，所以他还是毫不犹豫地点头，努力回应着好友们的期待。

他很快便再次听到了这句话。那一年后汉兵溃，郭威入城。大乱引发大饥，兵荒马乱之中，许多如沈家一般的普通民户陷入生存困境。阿郑与阿阮特意省下又送来的粮食，救了他的命。他望着眼前的朋友，更加卖力地点着头，觉得那个他还不能理解的“天下常平”的未来，就像手中捧着的窝窝一样，是那么甜、那么好。只可惜紧接着，突然出现的兄长就残忍而直接地将少年们的天真与良善统统撕个粉碎。
“乱世本就是弱肉强食，他们不死，我们怎么活？！”
沈义仁和他那帮后汉军中的兄弟，在战败后被郭威将军全城搜捕，他们在山野中流窜，若非饿极了绝不会下山。此时见了粮食，立马便红了眼，他们擒了阿郑和阿阮，就往郑家宅院冲去。这些流寇一路烧杀抢掠，不抢光粮食、烧尽宅院便决不罢休！
那一夜的郑家宅院起了一场漫天的大火。那火场中的哭喊和鲜血，让年少的沈义伦第一次恍然觉察，“天下常平，不知饥馑”这看似简单的八个字远比他曾想象得要重、要难。可也就是在他若有若悟的这一夜，他被同时剥夺了回头的权力。因为阿阮死了，兄长死了，很多人都死了。

沈义伦是在四年后离开家乡的。那一年朝生暮落之毒肆虐开封东部，他挣扎了、努力了，可却还是收到了阿郑的死讯。少年们一起活下去的约定终究落空，这一切都令沈义伦的心中生出一股巨大的悲哀，以及不可遏制地出走的冲动。——他不得不逼迫自己向前走，即使曾经的他总是跟在阿郑和阿阮的身后，即便这种前所未有的独行令他打心底里觉得惶恐。可他不想让少年们的约定变成一个彻头彻尾的笑话，而事到如今，也只有他能够继续向前走了。
于是年轻的沈义伦默默地背起了行囊，他要离开家乡、踏向远方。临别前夕，他再一次祭拜了好友。
“我们说好了，要让天下常平，不知饥馑。”
他对故友们许诺，然后带着前所未有的坚定转身离去。那时的他已经对前路的坎坷若有所悟，却仍然未料到，自己将为这句承诺，耗尽一生的时光。
en:
"We swear! We'll survive together, and make Ever-Normal for All! Everyone will be free from hunger!"
The first time Shen Yilun heard this vow, he was barely twelve or thirteen. Back then, he didn't truly grasp what "Ever-Normal for All" meant. Perhaps even Zheng Ruan, who'd said it with such bright laughter, didn't either. Yet something in those words called to the boy's heart. And since following Zheng E had long been his habit, he nodded fervently, eager to match his friends' hopes.

He heard the vow again the following year, when the Later Han army collapsed and General Guo Wei seized the capital. Chaos bred famine, and families like the Shens faced starvation, until A'zheng and A'ruan saved them with their own rationed grain. Clutching the coarse bun they'd given him, he nodded even harder. Ever-Normal for All now tasted as sweet as this humble bread. Then his elder brother shattered that innocence.
"The strong devour the weak in times like these! If they don't die, how do we live?"
Shen Yiren and his Later Han comrades, hunted by Guo Wei's forces after defeat, had been starving in the mountains. At the sight of food, they seized A'zheng and A'ruan, stormed the Zheng estate, and left only ashes and blood behind.
That night, the Zheng estate burned in a blazing inferno. The screams and blood opened Shen Yilun's eyes to the weight of those words, "Ever-Normal for All," far heavier and harder than he'd imagined. And as he began to understand, he lost the right to turn back: A'ruan was dead, his brother was dead, and so many others.

Four years later, Shen Yilun left home. The Dawn-to-Dusk had ravaged eastern Kaifeng, and despite his efforts, he'd received news of A'zheng's death. Their vow to survive together had crumbled, leaving the boy consumed by grief and a desperate urge to move forward. He had to force himself ahead, even though walking alone, after years of following A'zheng and A'ruan, terrified him. He refused to let their promise become a joke, and now, he was the only one left to carry it. So the young Shen Yilun packed his bags, ready to leave his hometown. The night before departure, he visited his friends' graves again.
"We swore to make Ever-Normal for All and everyone free from hunger." He whispered to the departed, turning away with newfound resolve. Though he sensed the trials ahead, he never imagined this vow would consume his entire life.

zh: 《高山流水》为中国十大古曲之一。原为一曲，自唐代以后，《高山》与《流水》分为两首独立的琴曲。曲谱初见于明代《神奇秘谱》。“高山流水”最先出自《列子·汤问》，传说伯牙善鼓琴，钟子期善听。伯牙鼓琴志在高山，钟子期曰：“善哉，峨峨兮若泰山。”志在流水，钟子期曰：“善哉，洋洋兮若江河。” 伯牙所念，钟子期必得之。子期死，伯牙谓世再无知音，乃破琴绝弦，终身不复鼓。

于是，红事、乔迁、高中、哪儿喜庆，哪儿就能看见她的身影。
吃得是油光水滑，膘肥体壮，浑身上下的毛儿，亮得能照见人影儿。
大伙儿瞧着她这副富态样儿都乐呵，打趣说它是吉祥猫。唤他“六六”，说是六六大顺，好兆头。
这“六六”一叫，就有好吃的等着它，六六自个儿更是乐开了花。
en:
Sixsan was clever from the start, her little head spinning faster than a windmill. 
She knew one thing for certain. When humans are happy, their hands loosen, and tasty treats always follow. 
So wherever there was celebration, be it weddings, new homes, exam successes, there was Sixsan, tail high, eyes bright. 
Her coat gleamed like polished mirror, fat and glossy from feasting. 
Everyone in the village adored her cheerful, well-fed look and called her the Lucky Cat. They named her "Sixsan" for smooth sailing and good fortune. 
And true enough, every time someone called her name, a delicious treat would be waiting. And Sixsan would turn into the happiest cat in the world.

今授刻丝之法，“通经断纬”需于毫厘间运筹，原以为繁复，初学当缓。未想一木匠之子，仅观半日，便有所悟。他取竹管数截，制成简易梭架，各色纬线依序置之，取用自如，织工大悦。
师言“道在民”，今日于此，心有所悟，实不负我暂搁孤云之行。大道泛兮，何必执于一处？心中之憾，已然释怀。
en:
Sixteenth of March, my trip to Luancheng has exceeded half a month.
Today I taught the method of silk tapestry, 'warp through, weft break,' requiring fine work within the breadth of a hair. I thought it complicated and expected beginners to be slow. Unexpectedly, a carpenter's son grasped it after only half a day. He took several bamboo tubes and made a simple shuttle frame, arranging the colored weft threads in order for easy access. The weavers were delighted.
The master said, 'The Way lies among the people.' My heart understands this today, and my rHeron at temporarily setting aside my Lone Cloud journey is truly released. The Great Way is vast; why cling to one place? The rHeron in my heart has already been laid to rest.

zh:
安史之乱后，家国支离，异族并起，蚕食着河西膏腴。张议潮常怀忠肝赤胆，他誓心归国，不忍看山河破碎，于是执槊而起，聚民为炬，建立归义军，并以燎原之势，于十三年间夺回四千里山河。归义军虽无唐廷兵马相援，但得河西百姓支持，军民一心，渴盼归唐，可谓万众同戈。
张议潮束甲归阙后，其侄张淮深接过重任，大阵乐的凯旋声犹在耳畔，盛唐残照拂过河西。然而凉州内外此时暗流汹涌，归义军的命运就如旗帜，在寒风中飘摇不定……
en:
After the An Lushan Rebellion, the nation was fragmented. Foreign tribes arose and encroached upon the fertile Hexi region. Zhang Yichao, ever loyal and courageous, vowed to restore the homeland. Unable to bear the sight of a shattered land, he took up his spear, rallied the people, and founded the Guiyi Army. Spreading as fast as a wildfire, they reclaimed four thousand miles of territory within thirteen years. Though lacking support from the Tang court, the Guiyi Army won the backing of Hexi's people. Soldiers and civilians unite, yearning to return to Tang. Truly, all people stood united in arms. 
After Zhang Yichao donned his armor and returned to the capital, his nephew Zhang Huaishen shouldered the responsibility. The triumphant sounds of grand victory music still echoed in their ears, the fading light of High Tang still brushed Hexi. Yet within and beyond Liangzhou, undercurrents surged. The fate of the Guiyi Army was like a banner, swaying uncertainly in the cold wind...

zh: 修面，又称剃面，是中国古代传统的美容方式之一。修面技艺起源于春秋战国时期，汉唐时期则出现了镊工，用丝线绞面。宋时则剃匠市井立，传播广泛，明清时期则有人挑着担子走街串巷，帮人清洁修容。修面技艺流传至今。
en: Known today as face threading, facial grooming is an ancient Chinese grooming art. The practice dates all the way back to the Spring and Autumn period. By the Han and Tang dynasties, specialized artisans were using fine silk threads to expertly pluck and contour facial hair. During the Song dynasty, street-side barbers became a staple of city life. By the Ming and Qing eras, wandering groomers were a common sight, carrying their tools on shoulder poles and walking from neighborhood to neighborhood offering a clean shave. Remarkably, this ancient craft is still practiced in parts of China today.

zh:
【天文·三】

【雪】

嘲王历阳不肯饮酒
李白

夜雪
白居易
已讶衾枕冷，复见窗户明。
夜深知雪重，时闻折竹声。

【雷】

雷
杜甫
巫峡中宵动，沧江十月雷。
龙蛇不成蛰，天地划争回。
却碾空山过，深蟠绝壁来。
何须妒云雨，霹雳楚王台。

闻雷
白居易
瘴地风霜早，温天气候催。
穷冬不见雪，正月已闻雷。
震蛰虫蛇出，惊枯草木开。
空馀客方寸，依旧似寒灰。

【虹】

晚晴
杜甫
返照斜初彻，浮云薄未归。
江虹明远饮，峡雨落馀飞。
凫雁终高去，熊罴觉自肥。
秋分客尚在，竹露夕微微。

江楼晚眺景物鲜奇吟玩成篇寄水部张员外
白居易
澹烟疏雨间斜阳，江色鲜明海气凉。
蜃散云收破楼阁，虹残水照断桥粱。
风翻白浪花千片，雁点青天字一行。

en:
【Astronomy · Three】

【Snow】

Mocking Wang Liyang for Refusing to Drink
Li Bai
The ground is white, the wind chill, snowflakes big as a hand.
You'd make Tao Yuanming laugh, not drinking from the cup you hold.
In vain you strum a zither, plant five willows for naught.
You wear the headcloth for show, what use are you to me?

Lodging with the Master of Hibiscus Mountain on a Snowy Night
Liu Changqing
At dusk, the blue mountains distant; in cold, the thatched hut poor.
At the brushwood gate, a dog barks; through wind and snow, one returns at night.

Night Snow
Bai Juyi
Already surprised by the cold of quilt and pillow, I see the window bright again.
Deep in the night, I know the snow is heavy, at times hearing the sound of breaking bamboo.

【Thunder】

Thunder
Du Fu
At midnight in Wu Gorge it stirs, on the Cang River, thunder in the tenth month.
Dragons and snakes fail to hibernate, heaven and earth clash in turmoil.
It rolls past empty mountains, coils up from sheer cliffs.
Why need it envy clouds and rain? Its thunderbolts strike the terrace of the King of Chu.

Hearing the Thunder
Bai Juyi
In the miasmal land, wind and frost come early; the warm weather hastens the season.
In the depth of winter, no snow is seen; by the first month, thunder is already heard.
Startled from hibernation, insects and snakes emerge; shocked from dormancy, grass and trees sprout.
Only my traveler's heart remains, still like cold ashes.

【Rainbow】

Clear Evening
Du Fu
The setting sun's slanting light first pierces through; thin clouds linger, not yet gone.
A river rainbow drinks bright from afar; gorge rain falls, its remnants fly.
Wild ducks and geese finally soar high; bears feel themselves grow fat.
At the autumn equinox, a guest still stays; bamboo dew glistens faintly in the evening.

Composing a Poem on the Fresh and Wondrous Scenery Seen While Gazing from a Riverside Pavilion at Dusk, Sent to Vice-Director Zhang of the Ministry of Water Resources
Bai Juyi
Pale mist and sparse rain part the slanting sun; the river's hue is bright, the sea air cool.
Mirages scatter, clouds withdraw, revealing broken towers; a fading rainbow over water lights a ruined bridge.
The wind churns white waves into a thousand blossoms; wild geese dot the blue sky in a single line.
Fine to capture with painting's reds and blues, I inscribe this poem to send to the Water Department郎.

扶摇一峰，以其近天之故，栖寄山人窥天之愿。
是故山中匠人穷百代之机巧，筑飞天之高城。彼时峰上，万枢运转之声不绝，九霄烝烝之灯不灭。若夫流云起，雾霭升，人影翩翾，穿于云间，果如天阙。扶摇之峰，确然其名。
及至城坠灯落，悲声动地，昔日憧憧天人，今日流民野鬼。泽葵依井，荒葛罥涂。飞天之试，付与东流。
时人谈及，无不惆惋。昔者山民无不举家登临，身近天穹一尺，犹似多窥天志一分。所谓天志，果真窥天则察耶？果真触天则得耶？莫若日日仰睹残垣，前事不忘，后事之师，天志或在其中矣
en:
Ascendant Peak, so near the heavens, became the place where the mountain folk pinned their longing to glimpse the sky.
And so the craftsmen of the mountains drew on the ingenuity of generations to build a towering city that reached toward the heavens. In those days, atop the peak, the turning of countless mechanisms never fell silent, and the lamps high among the clouds never went out. When the clouds drifted and the mists rose, figures moved to and fro among them, as if passing through the heavenly courts themselves. The mountain truly lived up to its name.
But when the city fell and the lights went out, grief shook the earth. Those who had once seemed almost heavenly became, before long, refugees and wandering dead. Marsh herbs grew by the wells, and wild vines choked the paths. The dream of flight was swept away downstream.
Whenever people speak of it now, none do so without sorrow. In former days, the mountain folk would bring their whole families to climb the peak. To stand but a foot closer to the sky felt as though one might glimpse a little more of Heaven's Will. But does peering into the heavens truly let one understand it? Does touching the heavens truly let one attain it? Better, perhaps, to look each day upon these ruined walls, to remember what has passed, and to take the past as a lesson for what comes after. Perhaps Heaven's Will is to be found there instead.

zh: 旧题晏婴撰，记其行事与谏诤之言，文辞雅驯，足为后世法。刘歆《七略》与班固《汉书·艺文志》列之于诸子略儒家，以其“以民为本、与民同乐”之旨近于孔氏。然《四库全书总目》以其以晏婴名冠，实为后人采撷其言行而成，疑非出自一人之手，故由子部儒家移入史部传记类，“庶得其实”。
en: Traditionally attributed to Yan Ying, this work records his conduct and his words of remonstrance; its prose is elegant and well-ordered, worthy of serving as a model for later ages. Liu Xin's Seven Summaries and Ban Gu's The Book of Han: Treatise on Literature placed it among the Confucian texts in the section on various schools of thought, on account of its guiding principle of "taking the people as the foundation and sharing joy with the people," which aligns it closely with the school of Confucius. However, the General Catalogue of the Siku Quanshu noted that, though the work bears the name of Yan Ying as its crown, it was in truth compiled by later hands gathering together his words and deeds, and was likely not the work of a single author. It was therefore moved from the Confucian subsection of the philosophers' section into the biographical subsection of the history section, so as to, in its own words, "more fitly accord with the truth."

zh:
显德元年的那场朝生暮落之灾改变了许多人的命运。除了孙愿、朱鱼、郑鄂、沈义伦……这些或多或少影响了太仓粟的人，更多的是翟煦这般的黎民百姓。
只是翟煦与其他人相比，多了一点运气。虽然他心中明白，自己被孙愿收为青溪弟子的缘由，完全是出于偶然。可是让人认命，尤其是让年轻人认命，从来不是一件容易的事。资质平凡的人，往往会将希望寄托于努力。于是在千愿坞进学的那近千个日夜里，翟煦夙兴夜寐、孜孜不倦。他希望自己至少可以证明，自己可以做得与师兄郑鄂一样好。可惜的是，青溪过去的愿弃之争，还有太多更久远的先例，早已证明，天赋是一道难以逾越的鸿沟，足以让普通人望其项背的心愿变得十足可笑。

孙愿离开开封后，翟煦也在灰心丧气地回到聆杏村。“我到底能做什么？”“我真的完全没有攻克朝生暮落之毒的希望？”——他反复追问着自己，迷茫而彷徨。可普通人永远是要为俗事和生活奔波的，故乡的境况并没有给他多少徘徊无措的时间。此时的聆杏村虽然已过了最难的时候，却仍是贫病交加、百废待兴。
作为唯一的青溪亲传，药材的种植与炮制、村民的收容与安置、沉疴与小恙的治疗…… 桩桩件件，都需要他。而在兢兢业业数年之后，翟煦忽然发现，聆杏村已在众人的努力下变了模样。他目瞪口呆地看着已日渐有序的百草堂、粥香萦绕的福田院，还有药材遍植的清心圃…… 直到几名过路的顽童打断了他的思绪。他们与他一样，都是经历了毒灾苦难的平凡人。他们的眼睛里有悲伤，有自艾，却也有希望。
“谢谢先生收留我和阿姊！”
“谢谢先生给我的阿娘看病！”
“等我长大了，我要像先生一样！”
简简单单的几句话，却瞬间如清泉般，令翟煦醍醐灌顶。望着身前的一双双眼睛，翟煦忽然明白自己能做什么、该做什么了。

于是又几年过去，太平书院在村南开设。已在太医署任职的翟煦向聆杏村，乃至全开封的百姓承诺，凡是有心向学的孩童，都可以来此免费受教。他还与同僚们一起，在长兴集兴建惠民和剂局，又编订《开宝本草》等书，尽力惠及百姓。
此时的翟煦已然明白，或许自己终其一生也无法在才学上超越师兄，更无法解决朝生暮落之毒，可是他却已不再执着。
“如果一件事，我倾尽全力也无法做到，那便做好眼前的。然后将它交给众人与未来，让千千万万个‘我’一同努力、一齐做到。”
翟煦在心中默念着，然后将视线投向不知名的远方。他的眼睛里有释然，有遗憾，却更有希望。
en:
The Dawn-to-Dusk Plague of the first year of the Xiande era reshaped countless lives, from Sun Yuan, Zhu Yu, Zheng E, and Shen Yilun, whose hands influenced the Woven Sunlight Granary of Plenty, to ordinary folk like Zhai Xu.
Yet Zhai Xu carried a sliver of luck others lacked, though he knew well that Sun Yuan's decision to take him as a Silver Needle disciple had been pure chance. Still, resigning to fate, especially for a young man, was never easy. Those with ordinary talents often cling to diligence, and so for nearly a thousand days in Wishing Cove, Zhai Xu rose before dawn and studied late into the night. He hoped to prove he could be as capable as his senior brother, Zheng E. But the past struggles within Silver Needle and even older precedents had long proven that talent was an insurmountable chasm, turning the aspirations of ordinary people into pitiful folly.

When Sun Yuan left Kaifeng, Zhai Xu returned to Apricot Village disheartened. "What can I even do?" "Is there truly no hope of curing the Dawn-to-Dusk poison?" He asked himself, adrift in confusion. But ordinary lives brook no time for aimless wandering. Though Apricot Village had survived its darkest days, it remained plagued by poverty and illness, every corner crying out for renewal. 
As the sole direct disciple of Clear Creek, Zhai Xu found himself responsible for everything: cultivating medicinal herbs, resettling villagers, and treating both chronic ailments and minor illnesses. After years of dedicated labor, he stared in awe at the transformed village: the orderly Herb Hall, the Charity Courtyard filled with the scent of congee, and the Stillheart Grove lush with medicinal plants... His thoughts were interrupted by passing children, all survivors of the plague like himself. Their eyes held sorrow and self-pity, but also hope.
"Thank you, Master, for taking in my sister and me!"
"Thank you for healing my mother!"
"When I grow up, I want to be like you, Master!"
These simple words struck Zhai Xu like a cool spring, jolting him awake. Gazing into those earnest eyes, he finally understood his purpose.

Years later, Taiping Academy opened south of the village. Zhai Xu, now serving in the Imperial Medical Academy, promised the people of Apricot Village, and all of Kaifeng, that any child eager to learn could study at the academy for free. With colleagues, he established the charitable pharmacies in Crosswind Bazaar and compiled texts like the Kaibao Herbal Compendium, striving to bring healing to the masses.
By then, Zhai Xu had accepted that he might never surpass his senior brother in learning, nor solve the mystery of the Dawn-to-Dusk poison. But he no longer obsessed over it.
"If there's a task beyond my sole ability, I'll focus on what's before me. Then leave the rest to the future and the efforts of thousands like me."
Zhai Xu murmured this to himself, gazing into the distance. His eyes held peace, lingering regret, but most of all, hope.
Young master... save me!

zh:
【国风·齐风】

鸡鸣

东方明矣，朝既昌矣，匪东方则明，月出之光。

还
子之还兮，遭我乎峱之间兮。并驱从两肩兮，揖我谓我儇兮。
子之茂兮，遭我乎峱之道兮。并驱从两牡兮，揖我谓我好兮。
子之昌兮，遭我乎峱之阳兮。并驱从两狼兮，揖我谓我臧兮。
著

俟我于庭乎而，充耳以青乎而，尚之以琼莹乎而。
俟我于堂乎而，充耳以黄乎而，尚之以琼英乎而。

东方之日

东方之日兮，彼姝者子，在我室兮。在我室兮，履我即兮。
东方之月兮，彼姝者子，在我闼兮。在我闼兮，履我发兮。
……
en:
【Airs of the States · Qi】

Crowing of the Rooster

The rooster has crowed, the court is full. It is not the rooster that crows, but the buzzing of flies.
The east is bright, the court is splendid. It is not the east that is bright, but the light of the moon.
The insects fly with a humming sound; gladly would I dream with you. The assembly will soon disperse; let not others hate you for my sake.
The Hunt
You are so agile, meeting me in the valley of Nao. Together we chase two boars; you bow to me, calling me swift.
You are so skilled, meeting me on the road of Nao. Together we chase two stags; you bow to me, calling me fine.
You are so strong, meeting me on the sunny side of Nao. Together we chase two wolves; you bow to me, calling me excellent.
Waiting at the Gate
Waiting for me at the gate, with earplugs of white silk, adorned with beautiful jade.
Waiting for me in the courtyard, with earplugs of green silk, adorned with sparkling jade.
Waiting for me in the hall, with earplugs of yellow silk, adorned with splendid jade.

Eastern Sun

The sun in the east, that beautiful maiden is in my chamber. In my chamber, she treads where I am.
The moon in the east, that beautiful maiden is in my inner room. In my inner room, she treads where I go.
……

小伙子含笑的眉眼被圈起，上扬的嘴角也被圈起——画上的是菩萨，画里的是他们的家。
en:
"The Bodhisattva on this sketch, there's an identical one in a temple in Chang'an. Seeing this, it's as if you've been to my hometown!" 
The yellowed mulberry paper slowly unfurled, pale dust fluttering down. Through the dense, tiny holes, the young man peered over, kind-eyed and gentle. 
"This was originally drawn by my grandfather, then passed to my father, and my father gave it to me. As for me… hey, when I marry and have children, I'll leave this paper to my kids too!" 
The young man's smiling eyes were circled, his upturned lips circled too, what was painted was the Bodhisattva, but within the painting was their home.

en:
1. Fun Competition - Guandan consists of 4 stages: Qualifiers, Group Stage, Semifinals, and Finals. The tournament will #Ydynamically enter stages#E based on the number of registered players.
2. #YQualifiers#E consist of rotating matches with Base Scores and target Bronze Tokens gradually increasing. Players who do not meet the Bronze Tokens threshold after each match are eliminated until 16 participants remain, from which the top 12 advance to the next stage.
3. At the start of the #YGroup Stage#E, Bronze Tokens from the Qualifier will be converted, #Ywith an upper limit of 2,000#E. Players at the same table then compete in 2 consecutive matches, and the top 8 advance to the next stage.
4. In the #YSemifinals#E, players at the same table also compete in 2 consecutive matches, and the top 4 advance to the Finals.
5. #YFinals#E consist of 2 consecutive matches to determine the winner.
