zh:
梨花树下，梨花飞舞。
石桌上沾了不少花瓣，花瓣间摆了一坛酒，坛边有两个画有柳叶纹的白瓷酒杯。
寒香寻已倒好了酒。

魏芷昔不同寒香寻客气。她仰头，第一杯酒下肚，总算觉得缓过神来。
这世上能使唤她去做埋尸骨这种活的……也只有对面这人了。
但没办法，谁叫自己欠了她一条命。

第二杯酒下肚。魏芷昔摸了摸石桌板上的长刀，上头还留有水渍。
狼山一战后，她有许久未提刀。昨日她本想着来找寒香寻喝喝酒，解解苦闷，没成想刚进山，就见寒香寻在后头提着个剑追赶一人。
 “拦他！”
“哦。“
飞星镖出手，那人弯膝倒地。寒香寻追至眼前，手起剑落，利落得很。
原来是要杀他。魏芷昔摸了摸腰间的长刀。
其实寒香寻若喊“杀他”，她出刀时，也断不会犹豫的。
但她不愿见血，而寒香寻懂她。所以这把刀，昨日并未见血。
她只是见寒香寻在河里清洗她的剑时，闲得慌，在一旁拿刀搅起几个漩涡……顺便收到了几个白眼。

第三杯酒下肚。
魏芷昔想，到了该走的时候了。
那契丹间谍死前，被她们套出了不少消息。北汉，朝堂……这些消息，叫她更加明白了今后的道路。
她得走得高些，再高些。站得足够高，才看得足够远。她要看那根节如何盘绕，看那腐朽如何生就，然后她要凭心中的刀，斩断这乱世中滋生恶的根。
而寒香寻心想，该是留下的时候了。
她得走得近些，再近些。走得足够近，才看得足够清。她要做眼前能做的事，护身后能护的人。她要救一人，再救一人，再救一人……救的人足够多，便也是一寸江湖，一片天地。
而且，那几人说的换脸，隐燕……她低头看向自己的双手。看来这身本事，该登台了。

酒杯落至桌面。二人对视一眼，然后起身，拜别。
三杯酒，半刻钟。她们好像什么都没说，又好像什么都说了。
这天下，需要渡舟，也需要及时雨。她们将分别，但她们也将在每一个得到庇护的人心中，反复相逢。
en:
Under the pear tree, pear blossoms fluttered in the wind. 
Many petals had fallen on the stone table. Between the petals was a jar of wine, and beside the jar were two white porcelain wine cups painted with willow leaf patterns. 
Han Xiangxun had already poured the wine. 

Wei Zhixi didn't stand on ceremony with Han Xiangxun. She tilted her head back, drank the first cup in one go, and finally felt relieved. 
The only person in the world who could order her to do something like burying bones... was the woman sitting across from her. 
But there was nothing she could do, she owed her a life. 

She drank the second cup. Wei Zhixi touched the long sword on the stone table, there were still water stains on it. 
She hadn't wielded a sword in a long time after the Wolf Mountain Battle. Yesterday, she had come to find Han Xiangxun to drink and relieve her boredom. Unexpectedly, as soon as she entered the mountain, she saw Han Xiangxun chasing someone with a sword. 
 "Stop him!" 
"Okay." 
She threw a flying star dart, and the man knelt down and fell to the ground. Han Xiangxun caught up, raised her sword, and struck, clean and decisive. 
So she had wanted to kill him. Wei Zhixi touched the long sword at her waist. 
In fact, if Han Xiangxun had shouted "Kill him," she would not have hesitated to draw her sword. 
But she hated seeing blood, and Han Xiangxun understood her. That's why the sword hadn't shed blood yesterday. 
She had just felt bored while watching Han Xiangxun wash her sword in the river, so she used her own sword to stir up a few eddies... and received a few eye-rolls in return. 

She drank the third cup. 
Wei Zhixi thought it was time to leave. 
Before the Khitan spy died, they had extracted a lot of information from him. About Northern Han, about the imperial court... This information made her more aware of her path ahead. 
She had to climb higher, even higher. Only when standing high enough could she see far enough. She wanted to see how the knots tangled, how decay took root, and then use the sword in her heart to cut off the roots of evil born in this chaotic world. 
Han Xiangxun, however, thought it was time to stay. 
She had to get closer, even closer. Only when getting close enough could she see clearly enough. She wanted to do what she could in the present, protect those she could behind her. She wanted to save one person, then another, then another... Saving enough people would also make a corner of the martial arts world, a world of her own. 
Moreover, what those people had said about face-swapping, about Hidden Swallow... She looked down at her hands. It seemed time to put her skills on display. 

The wine cups fell onto the table. The two exchanged a glance, then stood up and took their leave. 
Three cups of wine, half a quarter of an hour. It was as if they had said nothing, yet as if they had said everything. 
This world needs a ferry boat to cross the river, and it also needs timely rain. They would part, but they would meet again and again in the hearts of everyone they had protected.

zh:
大豆腐脑
大豆腐脑和豆腐脑虽只有一字之差，但其差别就像饱经风霜的中年人和少年人一般。少年人尚如白豆腐一般清白单纯，光滑如新，但大豆腐脑则是坑坑洼洼，只有咸口，没有甜口了。世上的豆腐哪有长长久久的年轻单纯，只有一碗不再年轻，遇到了虾皮，接纳了黄豆，带着黑菜讨生活的大豆腐脑。里头的豆腐口感粗粝，孔洞和皱褶中浸满了一辈子遇到的牵挂和遗憾。口感比起未经世事的豆腐脑，自是要丰富多了。
en:
4. Firm, Savory Tofu Pudding

It is only one word away from tofu pudding, but the difference feels like youth versus a weathered middle age. Youth is pale and pure, smooth as fresh-made tofu. The firm kind is pitted and uneven, and it is all savory now, no sweetness at all.

Nothing stays young forever, not even tofu. This bowl has grown up, topped with dried shrimp, soybeans, and pickled greens.

The tofu is rougher on the tongue. Its pores and creases seem to hold a lifetime of worries and regrets. Compared with ordinary tofu pudding, the texture and flavor are far more complex.

蒿野茫茫，鹿鸣无觅。石壁之上，旧痕留刻。
仙鹿赐救，是苍生一念所化耶？是天地偶生慈悲耶？幻梦难醒，唯思蒿里鹿踪。
en: Long ago in Liangzhou, a dying man in his delirium saw a deer looking down at him. When he awoke, he was healed. After much inquiry, he learned the legend of a celestial deer that would descend from the skies and save the suffering, granting them longevity. Thus, he revered the deer as an auspicious creature, calling it Everdeer. While there was no deer could be heard in the vast wilderness, old carvings remain on the stone walls. Was the celestial deer born from the desire to live or the compassion of the gods? The illusory dream lingers with the deer's tracks only present in memories.

李攸之决定抱养它时，脱口而出“牛墩”这个名字。
牛墩牛墩，顾名思义，是主人盼它长得像牛一样敦实。
这一点倒是没落空，牛墩打小就圆滚滚的，小短腿撑着一身肉，走起路来一扭一扭。
可就是有点……不大开窍。
别人家的狗听见主人唤名字，撒着欢儿就跑过来了。牛墩听见，先愣一愣，歪着脑袋想半天，然后慢吞吞地站起来。走到一半又忘了要干什么，干脆原地坐下，舔起了爪子。
路过的青溪弟子瞧了它一眼，摇摇头说这狗先天不足，是傻子。
李攸之不信邪，于是把牛墩抱起来，安慰道：“你别听他胡扯，你不笨，只是还没开智。”
可是，这狗到底哪天才能开智呢？
某日午后，牛墩趴在桃树下打盹。忽然，一颗又圆又大的桃子熟透了，从枝头落下来，不偏不倚，正中牛墩的脑门。
只听“咚”的一声闷响，牛墩醒了，眨巴了两下眼睛。
打那之后，它像变了个狗似的，吃得更多了，跑得更快了，叫得也更响亮了，就连眼睛都变得有神起来，再也没人说过它缺心眼。
李攸之寻思着，这一定……一定是仙桃的缘故！
再后来，牛墩便被抱到了藏书馆。李攸之相信，她的牛墩，一定能在此大放异彩。
en:
The moment Li Youzhi decided to take it in, the name "Stocky" leapt from her lips without a thought.
Stocky... the name said it all. Its owner hoped it would grow up as sturdy as an ox.
In that regard, at least, her hopes were not disappointed. Stocky had been round and plump since it was small, a chubby body balanced on four little stumpy legs, waddling from side to side with every step.
But it was, it had to be said, a little... slow to catch on.
Other people's dogs, upon hearing their name called, would come bounding over in a flurry of joy. Stocky, upon hearing its name, would first go blank, tilt its head to one side and think for a good long while, then heave itself to its feet at a leisurely pace. Halfway there, it would forget what it had been doing, and simply sit down where it stood and lick its paws.
A passing Silver Needle disciple glanced at it, shook his head, and declared the dog dim-witted from birth.
Li Youzhi refused to accept this. She gathered Stocky up in her arms and said by way of comfort: "Don't listen to his nonsense. You are not slow! You simply haven't come into your wisdom yet."
But when, in truth, would that day ever come?
One afternoon, Stocky was taking a nap beneath the peach tree. All at once, a peach, round, large, and fully ripe, fell from its branch and dropped straight down, landing squarely on Stocky's forehead.
With a dull thud, Stocky woke with a start and blinked.
From that day onward, it was as though a different dog had taken its place. It ate more, ran faster, barked louder, and even its eyes had taken on a new brightness. Not a soul ever called it dim-witted again.
Li Youzhi was certain of it. It could only have been... it must have been the doing of that blessed peach!
Not long after, Stocky was brought to the Archives. Li Youzhi believed that her Stocky would, without a doubt, show its full splendor there.

两人相互扶持着闯过一道道关。只是。老翁的背越来越佝偻，而千里烛依然沉默。
“你不敢吃馍，是因为当初你阿爷阿娘在卖你之前……”老头顿了顿。
”这一路，咱们爷俩虽然不亲厚，但我也知道，你是个好孩子。”
“孩子，别怕任何事，也别饿着自己。"
“我就到这儿了。以后，饿了，累了，就向水里去找饭吃。”
“下水之前，要试深浅。”
“听闻水里的月亮可以变成馍馍。真想知道是什么味道啊……”
“那首歌谣怎么唱的来着……月亮光光，快把……网张……吃个馍馍……娃娃……”
老翁的声音逐渐低沉，最终如月华般消散水中。
半晌，女孩的哭泣声传来，仿佛多年前那场永不停歇的雨。
en:
"Cough, cough... kid, care for a bun?" The old man gazed at the moon in the night sky. 
Relying on alms, the old man pulled Celestial Candle all the way west. They had no destination, just walked. 
At first, Celestial Candle was afraid of water, so the old man pushed her. Slowly, the girl dared to walk ahead, testing the river's depth with her feet. 
The two supported each other through pass after pass. Only, the old man's back grew more hunched, while Celestial Candle remained silent. 
"You're afraid to eat the bun because, back when your parents sold you..." The old man paused. 
"On this journey, though we aren't close, I know you're a good kid." 
"Kid, don't be afraid of anything, and don't go hungry." 
"My journey ends here. From now on, when you're hungry or tired, look for food in the water." 
"But test the depth before you go in." 
"They say the moon in the water can turn into a bun. I wonder what it tastes like..." 
"How does that song go again... 'Moonlight bright, cast your net right... eat a bun, little one...'" 
The old man's voice faded, finally dissolving into the water like moonlight. 
After a long while, the sound of the girl's weeping came, like a rain that never ceased years ago.

zh:
莺啼婉转，垂柳如丝。薰风沉醉，正好眠时。
桃花深处，城内文人赏景论诗，拉着睡道人品评。一人颂“绿柳垂丝拂面来，黄莺啼处百花开”，见睡道人点头，定是然也。另一人不服，又颂“玉辇不来春又老，声声诉与落花知”，睡道人再度点头，然也然也……一轮过后，众人不耐，问诸句之中，究竟以谁为最？道人不语，只一味点头……众人怒，拂袖而去。待到道人醒时，四下无人，桃枝散乱，唯莺啼几声，驴叫相和，正是“五更梦醒来堤岸，早有啼莺压满枝”。
en:
Warblers sing sweetly; willows trail like silk. Warm winds intoxicate; perfect weather for sleep.
Deep among the peach blossoms, the city's scholars admire the view and debate poetry, asking the Sleeping Daoist to judge their verses. One recites, "Green willow threads brush past the face; where orioles sing, a hundred flowers bloom." The Sleeping Daoist nods, surely in agreement. Another, unconvinced, recites, "The jade carriage comes no more and spring grows old; each cry tells the falling blossoms all it knows." Again the Daoist nods. Yes, yes... After a full round, the gathering loses patience and asks which verse is truly best. The Daoist says nothing and only continues nodding... Angered, they flick their sleeves and leave. When the Daoist wakes, no one remains. Peach branches lie scattered, a few warbler calls mingle with a donkey's bray, and the scene is perfectly captured: "At fifth watch, I wake from dreams beside the bank; already singing warblers weigh upon every branch."

西湖南岸，有山屏列焉，层峦耸翠，怪石参嵯，宛若屏障凌空，世人谓之南屏山。
其主峰曰慧日峰，下有幽居洞，窦穴玲珑，传声独远。
后周显德元年，吴越王钱弘俶于慧日峰下建慧日永明院，迎衢州道潜禅师开山说法。夫南屏山之胜，在其石骨嶙峋，空穴玲珑。每当暮霭沉沉，寺钟一鸣，山谷皆应，逾时方息。山与北岸孤山遥相对峙，一南一北，如天地之两极。孤山独屿临水，南屏屏障横陈，二者隔水相望，各极其胜。
en:
On the southern shore of West Lake stands a row of hills, tiered peaks rising in verdant splendor, strange rocks jagged and uneven, resembling a screen suspended in the sky, and people call it Nanping Hill.
Its main peak is called Wisdom Sun Peak, beneath which lies the Secluded Cave, its delicate and winding hollows carrying sound a long way.
In the first year of Xiande under Later Zhou, King Qian Hongchu of Wuyue built the Eternal Light Monastery under Wisdom Sun Peak, and invited Master Daoqian of Quzhou to preach. The beauty of Nanping Hill lies in its rugged stones and its delicate hollow caves. When the temple bell rings at dusk, the whole valley answers in echo, and it takes a long while to fade. Nanping Hill faces Lone Hill across the water, one to the south and one to the north, like the two poles of the world. Lone Hill rises alone on the waters, while Nanping stretches out like a screen; the two face each other across the water, each supreme in its own beauty.

zh: 又名《相府莲》、《想夫怜》、《丑儿》等。此曲为五绝，七律声诗，羽调曲也。传为王俭爱莲所作，《乐府诗集》引《古解题》日：“《相府莲》者，王俭为南齐相，一时所辟皆才名之士。时人以入俭府为莲花池，谓如红莲映绿水，今号‘莲幕’者自俭始。”亦有唐女无以此曲劝其夫量胜回心转意之说，此说或为讹传。
en: Also known as Lotus of the Minister's Residence, Longing for a Husband's Return, and The Unseen Grace, this piece is a five-line quatrain set to a seven-tone regulated verse, structured as a Yu-mode melody. Tradition attributes its composition to Wang Jian, famed for his love of lotus symbolism. The Yuefu Poetry Collection cites the Ancient Explanations: "The title Lotus of the Minister's Residence derives from Wang Jian's court, where he recruited only scholars of exceptional talent. Contemporaries likened his ministerial headquarters to a lotus pond, comparing its brilliance to'red lotuses reflecting emerald waters', thus originating the term lotus-adorned court." An alternative legend claims Tang women sang this melody to persuade their husbands to reconsider marital estrangement, though it is likely apocryphal.

多一事不如少一事。这世道，谁会来冒名顶替当个丘八？

“谢可久”会。
他是从死人堆里爬出来的。城破了，他的将军降了，他的战友没了，可老天却像和他开玩笑一样。让他活了下来。
活下来了，但这茫茫天地，已没有了他的来处，也没有他的去处。
所以当花完身上最后一分买酒的钱，他又把自己卖进了行伍里，用的是他队正的名字。
就好像，他还在。

……

“姓甚名谁？”
“周富贵。”
“入城作甚？”
“送信，家中有个远方的弟兄，叫赵铁，家住栾城布防，您看看……”他熟练地拿出个酒囊，送给这守城的兵士。
“行行行，进去吧。哪的酒这么香？”那卫兵拧开闻了闻，挥挥手让他进去了。
多一事不如少一事。这世道，谁家没点穷亲戚？

“周富贵”没有。
他爹娘死得早，死的时候连个正式的名都还没给他起。所以他参军的时候，用得还是个土名。
人都说赖名好养活。所以他总想，可能是名太赖，要不怎么老天都不肯收他走。
让他这个无牵无挂无家之人活下来，而那些有家有口有人牵挂的弟兄，却都死在了战场上？
他只能背上行囊，替这些兄弟们的遗书和粮饷，送到家人手中。去一个地儿，便换一个名。
就好像，他们都还在。

……

“你……姓甚名谁？”这次轮到他问别人了。
“我叫赵不易。”
“你大伯叫赵石？”
“咦？伯伯，你认得我大伯？我大伯参军好多年了，厉害着呢！”
他不认得赵铁，但他认得赵石。那是与他一道写下绝笔信的弟兄，是死在了晋安寨没能出来的弟兄。
栾城中家家织布，要找到赵家并不容易。但他看到这小孩的长相时，便知道找到了。
他掏出那封在他胸口放了许久的信，将它放到了赵不易手中，让他转交给赵石。
赵不易看了看手里血染的信封，又看了看眼前的斗笠男子，似是明白了什么。
“大伯……他……回不来了，对吗？”
他不知道如何回答这个问题，只好拍了拍赵不易的头，转身离开。
身后，是稚嫩的声音问他：”伯伯，你呢，你叫什么，我以后还能见到你吗？”
他随意挥了挥手，说了个名字，“丁献真。”
他记得那是个和赵不易一样的半大小孩，只是……也回不了家了。

又过了不知多久……
 
城门口，卫兵在例行询问出城的人。 
“姓甚名谁？”
“孟宽。”
“孟宽……去哪里？”
“去北边。” 
“去北边作甚？”
“找人，送信。” 
“孟宽”押了押新换的帽檐，混在人群中往北而去。 
他知道，还有许多人在在等这些名字回来，或者，等一个交代。
至于他自己？无人等的人，用不得名字。
en:
"Name?"
"Xie Kejiu."
"Where are you from?"
"Should be... Yingzhou."
"Should be?"

The clerk handling enlistment looked up and gave the man in front of him a once-over.
Height was fine. He looked young enough. Build... no obvious disability.
Good enough.

The clerk nodded, licked the tip of his brush, and wrote something down.
"Li Jingxing. Once you're in camp, you follow the rules. Got it?"
Best not to make trouble where there didn't need to be any. In times like these, who would steal someone else's name just to become a common soldier?

"Xie Kejiu" would.

He had crawled out from a heap of corpses. The city had fallen. His general had surrendered. His comrades were gone. And yet Heaven, as if making sport of him, had let him live.
He had lived, yes. But in this vast world, he no longer had anywhere to come from, or anywhere to go back to.

So after he spent his last coin on wine, he sold himself to the army again, this time under his squad leader's name.
As if that man were still here.

...

"Name?"
"Zhou Fugui."
"What are you entering the city for?"
"Delivering a letter. I've got a distant kinsman named Zhao Tie stationed with the Luancheng garrison. If you'll just take a look..."
As he spoke, he smoothly pulled out a wineskin and offered it to the guard.

"All right, all right. Go on in. Where'd you get wine this fragrant?"
The guard uncapped it, took a sniff, and waved him through.
Best not to make trouble where there didn't need to be any. These days, who didn't have some poor relative somewhere?

"Zhou Fugui" didn't.

His parents had died early, before they had even given him a proper name. So when he enlisted, all he had was the cheap little milk name they had called him by.
People said a worthless name was easier to keep alive. So he often thought maybe his name was too worthless. Why else would Heaven refuse to take him?
Why leave alive a man with no family, no ties, no one waiting for him, while all those brothers of his who had homes and people to miss them had died on the battlefield?

All he could do was shoulder his pack and carry their last letters and unpaid wages to the families they had left behind.
Everywhere he went, he used a different name.
As if they were all still here.

...

"And you, what's your name?"
This time, he was the one asking.
"My name is Zhao Buyi."
"Is your uncle Zhao Shi?"
"Huh? You know my uncle? He's been in the army for years. He's really something."

He did not know Zhao Tie.
But he knew Zhao Shi.

Zhao Shi was one of the brothers who had written their final letters beside him, one of the brothers who had died at Jin'an Fortress and never come back out.
Every household in Luancheng wove cloth, so finding the Zhao family had not been easy. But the moment he saw the boy's face, he knew he had found the right place.
He took out the letter he had carried against his chest for so long and placed it in Zhao Buyi's hands, telling him to pass it to Zhao Shi.
Zhao Buyi looked at the bloodstained envelope, then at the man in the bamboo hat before him, and seemed to understand.

"My uncle... he's not coming back, is he?"
He did not know how to answer.
So he only patted Zhao Buyi on the head and turned to leave.

Behind him, the boy's young voice called out:
"Mister, what about you? What's your name? Will I ever see you again?"
He lifted a hand without looking back and gave him a name at random.
"Ding Xianzhen."

He remembered that one.
About the same age as Zhao Buyi.
Only... he would never make it home either.

...

After who knew how long...
At the city gate, the guards were questioning people leaving the city as usual.

"Name?"
"Meng Kuan."
"Meng Kuan... where to?"
"North."
"What for?"
"Looking for someone. Delivering a letter."

"Meng Kuan" lowered the brim of his newly changed hat and followed the crowd heading north.
He knew there were still many people waiting for those names to return, or at least for word of what had become of them.
As for himself, no one was waiting.

And a man no one waits for has no use for a name.

zh:
他遇见我之前，已经被村里的八只猫拒绝遍了。我全看在眼里。
远远走来一个人，只凭脸上红一道白一道，我便知道准没别人。
别的猫不好惹，我就好惹了？我扬起爪子，准备吓唬吓唬他。
他果真忙用袖子遮住了脸，袖中却滚出一个烧饼来。
烧饼……？
不知怎的，等我回过神来，我已经吃完了一整个烧饼，还翻着肚皮，打着呼噜，任他抱回了家……
他日日为我下河捞最鲜的鱼，上市集挑最嫩的鸡。说来也怪，如他一般装束的人好像都很忙，他怎么可以天天守着我呢？
直到某天有个白胡子老头找上门来，说什么“晓山呐，你这成绩……”
从此，虽然白天我还是不缺好吃的饭，但夜晚不能窝在他的怀里睡觉了。
烛火幽幽，不知道他在读什么呢？这样对眼睛好不好？
我蹭蹭他的腿。原来比美味更令人依赖的，是彼此紧贴的温暖。
en:
Before he met me, he had already been rejected by all eight cats in the village. I saw it all.

A person approached from afar. Just by the red and white scratch marks all over his face, I knew it could be no one else.

If the other cats were not to be trifled with, did he think I would be an easy target? I raised my paw, ready to give him a good scare.

Sure enough, he hastily covered his face with his sleeve, but a baked sesame flatbread rolled out from within it.

A flatbread...?

Somehow, by the time I came back to my senses, I had already finished the entire flatbread, flipped belly-up, and started purring, letting him carry me all the way home...

Day after day, he would wade into the river to catch the freshest fish for me, and visit the market to pick the most tender chicken. It was rather strange. People dressed like him always seemed so busy. How could he afford to stay by my side every single day?

That was until one day, a white-bearded old man came knocking, saying something like, "Xiaoshan, your results..."

From then on, although I still lacked no delicious meals during the day, I could no longer curl up and sleep in his arms at night.

The candlelight flickers dimly. What could he possibly be reading? Is doing this good for his eyes?

I rub against his leg. It turns out that a shared, close warmth is even more addictive than delicious food.

en:
Master Zhong is a regular at Revelry Hall and a favored guest there. Lately, however, he has taken to muttering to himself, endlessly carrying on about..., insisting it's the soulmate who has captured his heart at first sight, demanding that Revelry Hall produce that person at once.
As if anyone like that could be conjured up. Since the Revelry Hall could offer no such person, he set out to search for them himself. The maidens of Velvet Shade did nothing to stop him; they only smiled and teased, "Still hunting for your soulmate, Master Zhong?"
With his heart in his throat and a stubborn breath caught in his chest, Master Zhong swore he would find this person no matter what. He dashed up and down the tower more than a dozen times before at last finding the little room where he had caught that dazzling glimpse. The door, it turned out, had been hidden behind a folding screen all along. No wonder he had searched in vain!
Overjoyed, he bypassed the screen and hurried inside, only to find the room empty.
Why was there only a chessboard left behind? The pieces had been put away; there was no telling if a player had yet to arrive, or if a game had just ended and they had already departed.

zh:
李筠给她做了她最爱吃的菜，招招手让她过来的那个下午，日光极好，她看向父亲的眼睛，那双眼睛比以往更柔和，她心想今日定不同父亲吵架了：“什么事？”
直到她听见那个荒唐的决定，她的父亲，要给她换个父亲。
“咋不行！你和慕容延钊不处得好！不是还叫他阿爹吗……我俩虽然有父女缘分，但合不来，你跟我也吃苦——”
“我是为你好。”

她不懂。
可比起这个，我想和你吃苦，反正也吃惯了。
以她的性子，是说不出这句话的，那个夜里，她赌气没有看一眼父亲，也没有看一眼弟弟，负气逃出了家。

她先是飞快地向前走，后来放慢了脚步，再后来，开始回头，在离开家的每一寸脚步中，她都没有怀疑过，有人会来寻她，起码爹总会来找她的吧。
可她没有等到任何人。

她离家越来越远了，走了一个时辰的时候，她的步子重得很，走到半日的时候，她忍着没有回头看，再往前走，先是愤怒变得冷却，之后火星似的期待一点一点失温，等她逃到墨山道之时。
她终于认清了，她被丢下了，她的脚走得生疼，她却没有流一滴眼泪。

她想，这条路真难走啊。
她想，这一路并不难走，难受的是她还相信有人会来找她，若是不这么想，路便好走了许多。

那日后，便不要这样想了。
期待是比路更难走的东西。
en:
It was a sunny afternoon when Li Jun cooked her favorite dishes and beckoned her over. Gazing into her father's softer-than-usual eyes, she decided she wouldn't quarrel with him today. "What is it?"
Then she heard the absurd proposal: Her father had decided to give her a new father.
"Why not? You get along with Murong Yanzhao! You even call him 'Father'... We're father and daughter by fate, but we clash. You suffer with me..."
"I'm doing this for your own good."

She didn't understand.
But more than that, she wanted to share his hardships. She was used to them by now.
Her pride wouldn't let her say this. That night, she stormed out without glancing at her father or younger brother.

At first, she marched swiftly, then slowed, then began looking back. With every step, she never doubted someone would come for her. Surely her father would follow.
But no one came.

Two hours passed. Her legs felt leaden. After half a day, she forced herself not to turn around. As she trudged toward Mohist Hill, her anger cooled, and the spark of hope in her chest died.
Finally, she accepted the truth: she'd been abandoned. Her feet ached, but she shed no tears.

This road is so hard to walk, she thought.
No, it isn't the road. It's the waiting that hurts. The hoping. If I could just stop expecting someone to come for me, maybe the road wouldn't feel so long. 

From that day on, she stopped hoping. Hope, she realized, is harder to carry than the road itself.
An embroidered handkerchief.
Let go of me!

zh:
【桓公第二】

○元年，春，王正月，公即位。
桓无王，其曰王何也？谨始也。其曰无王何也？桓弟弒兄，臣弒君，天子不能定诸侯，不能救百姓，不能去以为无王之道，遂可以至焉尔。元年有王，所以治桓也。继故不言即位，正也。继故不言即位之为正何也？曰先君不以其道终，则子弟不忍即位也。继故而言即位，则是与闻乎弒也。继故而言即位，是为与闻乎弒何也？曰先君不以其道终，己正即位之道而即位，是无恩于先君也。
○三月，公会郑伯于垂。郑伯以璧假许田。
会者，外为主焉尔。假不言以，言以，非假也。非假而曰假，讳易地也。礼，天子在上，诸侯不得以地相与也。无田则无许可知矣。不言许，不与许也。许田者，鲁朝宿之邑也。邴者，郑伯之所受命而祭泰山之邑也。用见鲁之不朝于周，而郑之不祭泰山也。
○夏，四月，丁未，公及郑伯盟于越。
及者，内为志焉尔。越，盟地之名也。
○秋，大水。
高下有水灾曰大水。
○冬，十月。
无事焉，何以书？不遗时也。春秋编年，四时具而后为年。

二年，春，王正月，戊申，宋督弒其君与夷及其大夫孔父。
桓无王，其曰王何也？正与夷之卒也。孔父先死，其曰及何也？书尊及卑，春秋之义也。孔父之先死何也？督欲弒君而恐不立，于是乎先杀孔父，孔父闲也。何以知其先杀孔父也？曰，子既死，父不忍称其名；臣既死，君不忍称其名，以是知君之累之也。孔氏父字，谥也。或曰：其不称名，盖为祖讳也，孔子故宋也。
○滕子来朝。
○三月，公会齐侯、陈侯、郑伯于稷，以成宋乱。
以者，内为志焉尔，公为志乎成是乱也。此成矣，取不成事之辞而加之也。于内之恶，而君子无遗焉尔。
○夏，四月，取郜大鼎于宋，戊申，纳于太庙。
桓内弒其君，外成人之乱，受赂而退，以事其祖，非礼也。其道以周公为弗受也。郜鼎者，郜之所为也。曰宋，取之宋也。以是为讨之鼎也。孔子曰:"名从主人，物从中国"，故曰郜大鼎也。
○秋，七月，纪侯来朝。
朝时，此其月何也？桓内弒其君，外成人之乱，于是为齐侯、陈侯、郑伯讨，数日以赂。己即是事而朝之。恶之，故谨而月之也。
○蔡侯、郑伯会于邓。
○九月，入杞。
我入之也。
○公及戎盟于唐。
○冬，公至自唐。
桓无会，而其致何也？远之也。

……
en:
【Duke Huan, Year 2】

○Year 1, Spring, the King's first month, the Duke assumed the throne.
Huan had no king; why does it say "King"? It is to be cautious at the beginning. Why does it say "no king"? Huan, as a younger brother, killed his elder brother; as a minister, he killed his ruler. The Emperor could not settle the feudal lords, could not rescue the commoners, and could not remove [the evil], thinking there was no way of the King, and thus this could come to pass. In the first year, there is "King," so as to govern Huan. When succeeding after a wrongful death, one does not speak of assuming the throne; this is correct. Why is not speaking of assuming the throne after a wrongful death correct? It is said: when the former ruler did not end his life by the proper Dao, the son and younger brother cannot bear to assume the throne. If one speaks of assuming the throne after a wrongful death, then one was complicit in the killing. Why is speaking of assuming the throne after a wrongful death being complicit in the killing? It is said: when the former ruler did not end his life by the proper Dao, and one rectifies the way of assuming the throne and then assumes it, this shows no gratitude toward the former ruler.
○Third Month, the Duke met with the Earl of Zheng at Chui. The Earl of Zheng used a jade disc to exchange for the fields of Xu.
"Meeting" means the other party took the lead. "Exchange" is not spoken of with "used"; saying "used" means it was not an exchange. It was not an exchange, yet it is called an exchange, to conceal the swapping of lands. According to ritual, when the Son of Heaven is above, feudal lords may not give lands to one another. Without fields, it is clear that Xu was not permitted. Not mentioning Xu means not granting Xu. The fields of Xu were the city where Lu lodged when attending court. Bing was the city where the Earl of Zheng received the mandate to sacrifice to Mount Tai. This shows that Lu did not attend court at Zhou, and Zheng did not sacrifice to Mount Tai.
○Summer, Fourth Month, Dingwei day, the Duke and the Earl of Zheng盟ed at Yue.
"And" means the intention was internal. Yue is the name of the place of the盟.
○Autumn, Great Flood.
When high and low places both suffer water disasters, it is called a great flood.
○Winter, Tenth Month.
There were no events; why record it? To not omit the season. The Spring and Autumn Annals are arranged by years; only when all four seasons are complete does it constitute a year.

Year 2, Spring, the King's first month, Wushen day, Song Du killed his ruler Yuyi and his Doctor Kong Fu.
Huan had no king; why does it say "King"? It is to rectify the death of Yuyi. Kong Fu died first; why does it say "and"? Recording the noble and then the lowly is the principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Why did Kong Fu die first? Du wanted to kill the ruler but feared he would not succeed, so he first killed Kong Fu, for Kong Fu was an obstacle. How do we know he first killed Kong Fu? It is said: when a son has died, the father cannot bear to speak his name; when a minister has died, the ruler cannot bear to speak his name; from this we know the ruler was implicated by him. Kong was the surname, Fu the style name, and it is a posthumous title. Some say: not speaking his name is to avoid the ancestor's taboo, for Confucius was originally from Song.
○The Viscount of Teng came to court.
○Third Month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Marquis of Chen, and the Earl of Zheng at Ji, to complete the disorder of Song.
"To" means the intention was internal; the Duke's intention was to complete this disorder. This was already completed, yet the wording of "not completing the matter" is applied to it. Regarding internal evil, the noble man does not omit it.
○Summer, Fourth Month, took the great tripod of Gao from Song; Wushen day, presented it in the Grand Temple.
Huan killed his ruler internally, completed others' disorder externally, accepted bribes and withdrew, to serve his ancestor—this is not ritual. His way is that the Duke of Zhou would not accept it. The Gao tripod was made by Gao. Saying Song means it was taken from Song. This is considered the tripod of punishment. Confucius said: "Names follow the master, objects follow the Central States," so it is called the great tripod of Gao.
○Autumn, Seventh Month, the Marquis of Ji came to court.
Courts are recorded by season; why is this one by month? Huan killed his ruler internally, completed others' disorder externally, and then for the Marquis of Qi, the Marquis of Chen, and the Earl of Zheng, he punished, counting the days with bribes. Having done this, he came to court. Despising him, therefore it is carefully recorded by month.
○The Marquis of Cai and the Earl of Zheng met at Deng.
○Ninth Month, entered Qi.
We entered it.
○The Duke and the Rong盟ed at Tang.
○Winter, the Duke arrived from Tang.
Huan had no meetings, yet why is his arrival recorded? To show it was distant.

因苍日日纠缠授武之事，青便许苍每日可打架五场，只不过皆需由青指定敌手。后苍居处十里之内地痞流氓，皆望风而逃，缘此一事，苍的体魄锻得愈发强健。
到授武之时，青教授起来不拘一格，苍学起来，亦是不拘一格，由此苍的武功旁人全然看不出路数，竟罕逢敌手。待青独自返回不见山，苍留于一庙宇中，又学了醮仪、傩舞等一应杂术，更特意为师父学会了打铁花。他将这些技法皆融于自身武学，期待着下一次再与师父交手。
en:
Goshawk grew up homeless. He lived on the streets, and fighting was how he survived. Once, he tried to rob Halcyon of Mohist Hill. Halcyon caught him and took him in as a disciple instead.
After that, Goshawk pestered Halcyon every day to teach him martial arts. Halcyon finally gave in: five fights a day, every day, and Halcyon would choose every opponent. Before long, the local thugs all kept their distance, and Goshawk only grew stronger.
Halcyon did not teach by the book, and Goshawk did not learn by the book either. So Goshawk's martial arts did not look like any familiar school. His moves were hard to read. That was why he so rarely met an equal. Later, Halcyon returned alone to Hidden Mountain, while Goshawk stayed on at a temple. There, he learned Taoism rituals, Nuo dance, and other odd skills. He even learned how to strike iron flowers for the sake of his master. In time, he made all of it part of his own martial arts. Since then, he has waited for the day he can cross hands with Halcyon again.

【Airs of the States · Airs of Chen】

Wanqiu

You dance so gracefully, on top of Wanqiu. Truly you stir emotion, yet there is no hope.
They beat the drums, at the foot of Wanqiu. No winter, no summer, holding their egret feather fans.
They strike the earthen jars, on the road of Wanqiu. No winter, no summer, holding their egret feather banners.

The White Elm at the East Gate

The white elm at the east gate, the oak at Wanqiu. The son of Zizhong dances beneath them.
On a fine morning chosen, to the southern plain. Not spinning their hemp, they dance in the market.
On a fine morning they go, gathering and moving on. I see you like a mallows flower, you give me a handful of pepper.

zh:
河神祠的大殿中，张彦霖不知疲倦地刻着牌位。满室的神祇，满室的死寂，只有楔子打入木头的声音，不慌不忙，不紧不慢，“笃——笃——笃——”

“河伯大禹”“河伯李冰”“河伯王景”“河伯……张……”每次刻到这姓氏，张彦霖的手总会慢一分。某个名字，他总会刻一个，再毁一个。刻是为了纪念，毁是为了忘却：忘却那个想要离家闯荡江湖的少年，忘却塞北的风沙与江南的桃花，忘却那想要逃避一切的自己。

与故人的约定，言犹在耳……可一身残躯，两鬓白发，以此残躯，又当……如何？不是所有绝望时，都能遇到朱鱼，这样的泥菩萨，世上又怎会有第二个。“笃——笃——笃——”

万古一人殿的大门，被人打开了。
en:
Within the Hall of the River Master, Zhang Yanling carved tablets, tireless and unceasing. A hall filled with deities, drowned in deathly silence. Only the steady sound of the chisel striking wood remained, neither hurried nor slow. 

"Tok, tok, tok..."

"River Master Yu the Great."

"River Master Li Bing."

"River Master Wang Jing."

"River Master... Zhang..."

Each time he reached that surname, Zhang Yanlin's hand would falter, just slightly. Some names he carved, then destroyed. Carved to remember, destroyed to forget. To forget the boy who had once dreamed of roaming the jianghu. To forget the northern deserts and the southern peach flowers. To forget himself who had once tried to run from everything.

The promises made to old friends still echoed faintly in his ears, but what could he do now, with a broken body and hair turned white? Not everyone, in their darkest hour, is lucky enough to meet someone like Zhu Yu. A clay bodhisattva like her, how could the world ever produce another?

"Tok, tok, tok..."

The heavy doors of the Eternal Solitude Hall creaked open.

江湖儿女快意恩仇，章阿狗没有仇要报，却记着那块冒着烟气的烧饼和那五文捂得热乎乎的铜钱。于是每次得了银钱，都取其中几文置入钱袋，攒着攒着，是时候了，他赴葱王坪来。
en:
When Zhang Gou first stepped into the jianghu, he quickly learned that beneath all the romanticized swordplay and poetry lay the harsh reality of putting food on the table. He learned how to beg, how to steal, and how to hoard his coins. But he also learned to remember every single act of kindness, waiting for the day he could repay them.
While others in the jianghu were obsessed with bloody vengeance, Zhang Gou had no enemies. Instead, he just remembered a steaming hot flatbread and the five warm copper coins pressed into his hand. Every time he scraped together some silver, he slipped a few coins into this bag. Now that he finally has enough, he's heading to Crownleek Terrace to pay his debt.

zh:
大侠近来可好？
有一份心意想送与大侠。为免寄送延误，还请先行[<LINK id='link' color='#8c5823' url='https://research-game.163.com/htmls/46rzpk/paper.html?uid={uid}&role_id={pid}&server={hostnum}' is_underline='true'>点此留下信址</LINK>]。待我细细说来：
写这封信，是想给你报个喜。多亏你先前帮忙，我才有了支起摊子的本钱，在开封南郊的麦香集里寻了个落脚处。当初从家里出来时，哪敢想有今日……
爷爷常说，谢人不能只挂在嘴上。想来想去，我把近日攒下的钱寄回富平老家，用大侠的名义承包了五亩柿子地，托爷爷和乡亲们照看。爷爷说，要让你瞧瞧，特意让村里的老画师给画了下来，我都能想象后头红彤彤的模样了！
不过今年老家的天儿有些邪乎……又是旱又是涝的没断过，八成会影响收成……等到了做柿饼的时候，总要送你些尝尝，可能不多，但都是乡亲们的心意。不知大侠住在何处？一定包得仔仔细细的给你送去！
<IMAGE id='im1' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/6937d9e87c343173e30ea49fSxCFdEdD07' size='1810*2704' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>
en:
Dear Wanderer,
How are you? I have a small token of my gratitude for you. To avoid any delay in its arrival, please press [<LINK id='link' color='#8c5823' url='https://research-game.163.com/htmls/46rzpk/paper.html?uid={uid}&role_id={pid}&server={hostnum}' is_underline='true'> to register your mailing address</LINK>] first. Allow me to explain:
I write with glad tidings. Thanks to your help, I've set up my stall at the Wheatwind Bazaar in Kaifeng Suburbs-South. When I left home, I never dreamed such a day…
Grandfather always said gratitude must be more than words. So I've sent my savings back to Fuping, my hometown, to lease five mu of persimmon groves in your name. Grandfather and the villagers tend them. He insisted on having the old painter paint them for you. I can already imagine the fiery red blaze!
But the weather's been cruel this year, drought and flood by turns. The harvest would likely suffer…
When the dried persimmons come, I'll send you some. Not much, perhaps, but grown from honest hearts. Where do you lodge? I'll package them with care and have them delivered.

1.基础操作
游侠通过选择流派搭配话术卡、妙语卡、箴言卡组建卡组。在对战期间，拖动手中卡牌到任意区域可以打出对应的卡牌。

当对决进入#Y加时环节#E，将全体弹幕加速，并且双方三路每秒持续损失心防。

#Y· 口出狂言#E
#Y快攻流#E，命中心防可叠鼓舞层数，每层增加话术卡攻击；满层后定期免费出牌。
#Y· 大力扎心#E
#Y绕路流#E，话术卡碰撞时可绕至相邻路继续前进，每次通过暗度陈仓绕路成功将降低对方存在感，降低三次将秒杀对方卡牌。
#Y· 气人杠精#E
#Y成长流#E，击败敌方话术卡可提升思路点回复速度及上限，积累优势后一击制胜。
#Y· 废话连篇#E
#Y防守流#E，话术卡对撞后产生废话卡堆在心防前；积累到位后利用箴言卡一次性爆发清场。
en:
1. Basics
Choose a Path and combine Gab Cards, Quip Cards, and Maxim Cards to build your deck. During battle, drag a card from your hand to any area to play it.

2. Victory
Both sides have #Ythree Inner Bastions#E: #YValour, Poetics, and Discernment#E. Reduce #Yany of your opponent's Inner Bastions#E to zero to claim victory. You lose if any of your own Inner Bastions reaches zero and you take inner damage.
When #YOvertime#E begins, the verbal barrage accelerates, and all three Inner Bastions on both sides continuously take damage every second.

3. Paths
#Y· Bluster#E
#YBlitz Tactics#E: Hitting Inner Bastions grants stacks of Cheer, boosting Gab Card attack. At max stacks, periodically play cards for free.
#Y· Provocation#E
#YFlanking Tactics#E: When Gab Cards clash, they can detour to an adjacent lane. Each successful detour reduces the opponent's Presence; triggering this 3 times instantly destroys the opponent's card.
#Y· Rebuttal#E
#YGrowth Tactics#E: Defeating enemy Gab Cards increases the recovery rate and cap of Inspiration Points. Build your advantage to seize victory in one strike.
#Y· Filibuster#E
#YBulwark Tactics#E: Gab Card clashes generate Fluff Cards that pile up before your Inner Bastions. Once accumulated, unleash a Maxim Card for a massive board-clearing burst.

zh:
西域人饲养和使用骆驼的历史非常早。《史记·匈奴列传》记载：“唐虞以上，有山戎、猃狁……其奇畜，则橐驼、驴……”这里的橐驼即骆驼。
作为一种“奇畜”，先秦时西域各国已将骆驼当作贡物进献中原王朝。
至唐时以骆驼代步极为常见。骆驼可负重千斤，日行二三百里，且能识途。
商队多以骆驼为载具，穿越沙海。

The Western Regions have a long history of raising and using camels. Records of camels can even be found in ancient tomes such as the Records of the Grand Historian, which mentions them among "rare beasts" alongside donkeys.

By the pre-Qin era, the kingdoms of the Western Regions were already offering camels as tribute to the Central Plains. By the Tang dynasty, riding them had become commonplace. 

A camel can carry immense burdens, travel vast distances in a single day, and unfailingly find its way across the desert. It is the lifeline of every caravan crossing the sea of sand.

zh:
绕过殿宇重重，终于让我寻得一处僻静角落。
墙外是禁中森严，墙内却是别有洞天——好一处皇家园林！我走南闯北，自认见过的景致不少，可此地的奇花异草，许多竟连名字都叫不上来，珍禽悠然踱步其中，见我这生人亦不惊慌，想来是过惯了富贵日子。
苑中春光摇曳，老树婆娑，也不知见过几代君王，听过多少秘闻。年年岁岁，这些花草树木开得一般葱茏，可坐在这园子里赏景的人，却换了一茬又一茬——这满园春色，究竟是为谁而开呢？
……嗨，想这些作甚？我一个歇脚看热闹的，倒替这满园芳菲伤感起来了。
en:
Passing hall after hall, I finally found a quiet corner. Outside the walls, the inner palace is tightly guarded. Inside, though, it feels like another world entirely, a royal garden in full bloom. I've traveled far and seen plenty of sights, yet many of the strange flowers and plants here are ones I can't even name. Exotic birds linger unbothered, not the least bit startled by a stranger like me. They must be used to living well.
Springlight drifts through the grounds and the old trees sway, as if they've watched generations of rulers come and go, and heard more secrets than anyone should. Year after year, the flowers and trees return just as lush, but the people who sit here to admire them are replaced again and again. So who is all this spring beauty meant for, after all?
But why am I dwelling on that? I'm only here to rest my feet and take in the sights, yet I've somehow grown melancholy over all this bloom.

zh: 世皆知龙为神物，兴云布雨，或飞在天，或潜入渊，或战于野。问其形状，人人能言，闻何处得见，则人人哑然。又有鲤鱼跃龙门，过而化龙之说。余少时颇疑之，尝至龙门，坐候十日，水声日夜不绝，而鳞爪杳然，
en: We all know the dragon as a divine beast, a master of clouds and rain. It ascends into the heavens, plunges into the lightless abyss, and thrashes wildly across the untamed wilderness. Ask anyone what a dragon looks like, and they will readily paint you a picture with words; but ask where they have actually seen one, and a profound silence falls. Then there is the old legend: any carp that leaps the Dragon Gate will ascend into a dragon. In my youth, I scoffed at this tale. I once sat at the foot of the Dragon Gate for ten days and nights, waiting. I heard nothing but the ceaseless, deafening roar of the rushing falls. Never once did I glimpse a single scale or claw.

zh:
阿爷阿娘敬启
儿在外漂泊多年，回首往昔，年少时离乡，心怀壮志，然风雨飘摇，路途艰辛，至今已然在悬泉驿安定。此地大漠连天，壮美奇绝，然乌鸟思乡，久萦心头。
阿爷年事已高，望平日多加珍重，勿劳心力。阿娘，冬日将至，院中红柿将熟，万望莫悉数摘尽，留一二予鸟雀，亦添冬日意趣。
尤记儿时，阿娘所做栗子糕软糯香甜，至此难忘。若有空暇，盼阿娘寄些至河西悬泉驿，以慰儿思乡之情。

敬颂钧安
儿某拜上
en:
Dear Father and Mother, 
Leaving home young with ambitious goals, I now settle at Celestial Spring Station after years adrift on this arduous journey. The desert stretches vast and majestic, yet this wandering bird still dreams of home. 
Father, you grow older—please take care and rest well. Mother, as winter nears, the persimmons in the yard will ripen. Leave a few for the birds, to sweeten the cold days. 
I still remember the chestnut cakes you made, soft and sweet—unforgettable. If you can, send some to Celestial Spring Station, to ease my homesick heart. 

Best regards 
Your son

zh:
今撰《摹吴道玄笔法要诀》，字字从历代画史中出，凡十有四则，务求简白：
一、立意
思其洛阳天宫寺壁上龙须戟张，方得气概。
二、执笔 
五指撮管如握刀，悬腕抵几，使全身力贯毫端。昔东坡谓：「道子运笔如庖丁解牛」，此之谓也。
三、勾线
起笔若折钗股，行笔似风过林，收笔类箭离弦。莼菜条法：中锋直下，圆转处不可生圭角。
四、衣纹
吴带当风，全在提按：人物疾行时，衣带翻飞处用笔轻疾；端立凝神时，襟袖垂坠处墨痕沉厚。
五、开面 
天王力士，颧骨须用斧劈皴；菩萨天女，蛾眉当以游丝描。点睛尤忌死黑，尝闻道玄画眸子，以淡墨渗朱砂，远望炯然如生。
六、设色
焦墨薄彩：色不过五，青绿施于衣带，赭石染就肌肤，金粉惟点法器。色不掩线，线不为色囚。
七、配景 
画火焰，勾三重蓝本：内层朱磦作底，中层胭脂扫掠，外沿轻施金边。观者觉热浪灼面，方称妙手。
八、避忌
四病不可犯：  
一曰臃：筋肉无骨； 
二曰僵：衣纹板滞；  
三曰浊：设色淹线；
四曰怯：神采萎靡。
en:
I now compile the Guide to Wu Daoxuan's Brushwork, with every word drawn from historical painting treatises. Totalling fourteen rules, I seek to make them clear and simple:
One, Conception. Imagine the dragons on the walls of the Tiangong Temple in Luoyang, their whiskers bristling and halberds drawn; only then can you capture the spirit.
Two, Holding the Brush. Pinch the shaft with five fingers like gripping a knife, suspend the wrist and brace against the table, channeling your entire body's strength to the brush tip. Su Dongpo once said, "Daozi wields the brush like a legendary butcher carving an ox." This is exactly what he meant.
Three, Outlining. Start the stroke like a bent hairpin, move the brush like wind through a forest, and finish like an arrow leaving the bowstring. The water-shield leaf method requires bringing the centered tip straight down, turning smoothly without sharp angles.
Four, Folds of Clothing. "Wu's drapery riding the wind" relies entirely on lifting and pressing. When a figure walks swiftly, the strokes for fluttering ribbons must be light and fast; when they stand still in thought, the ink traces of hanging sleeves must be heavy and deep.
Five, Rendering Faces. For Heavenly Kings and strongmen, cheekbones require axe-cut texture strokes; for Bodhisattvas and celestial maidens, delicate eyebrows should be drawn with gossamer lines. When painting eyes, strictly avoid lifeless black. I have heard that when Daoxuan painted pupils, he infused light ink with cinnabar: from afar, they looked vibrantly alive.
Six, Coloring. Burnt ink and thin pigments. Use no more than five colors: apply blue and green to robes, dye the skin with ochre, and use gold dust only for ritual implements. Colors must not obscure the lines, nor should lines be imprisoned by colors.
Seven, Backgrounds. To paint flames, draft a threefold blueprint. Use vermilion as the base in the inner layer, a sweep of carmine in the middle, and lightly apply a golden edge on the outside. Only when viewers feel a wave of heat on their faces can you be called a master.
Eight, Taboos. Four flaws must never be committed. First, bloatedness: flesh without bones. Second, stiffness: rigid folds of clothing. Third, muddiness: colors drowning out the lines. Fourth, timidity: a withered spirit.
Chai Sansheng

zh:
契丹贼寇攻入开封城的那日，倪老山正在千里之外的崖壁之上与人比武。
“不都说你入了鬼市，成了朱佑生的座上宾？”江南老怪斜卧在青松之间，揶揄打趣，“怎还有功夫来会我这老友？”
长剑出鞘，倪老山大笑道：“天大地大，武字最大！”

那场大战，二人剑去刀来，直斗了三天三夜都未分胜败。
最后还是江南老怪接到一飞鸽传书，称要回去处理门中事务，倪老山才意犹未尽地收手。
他这一生，最好武斗。与朱佑生相识，源于一场比试。入鬼市子，起初也不过是想同那的怪人们切磋比武。但日子久了，与那些人相处多了，渐渐也觉出些武斗之外的乐趣。
“小朱好茶，小八好酒。”行至开封城外的时候，倪老山手里提着给大家伙带的吃食，“一走就是三四天，那几位别恼我才好。”
但他万万没想到，再也没人会恼他了。

五年过去了，十年过去了，十五年过去了……倪老山还是从前那副嘻嘻哈哈的模样。但他再也不与人比武了。
而每当夜深人静的时候，他会敛起那张笑脸，遥遥望向长眠冢的方向。
“放心吧，这次，我会看好这儿的。”
en:
The day Khitan invaders stormed Kaifeng, Ni Laoshan was locked in a duel atop a cliff miles away.
"Rumor says you joined the Ghostlight Market and became Zhu Yousheng's honored guest," the Jiangnan Creepy teased, reclining against a pine tree. "Why waste time with an old friend like me?"
Drawing his long sword, Ni Laoshan laughed. "Heaven and earth may be vast, but martial arts reign supreme!"

Their battle raged for three days and nights, sword and blade clashing without end. 
It was only when the Jiangnan Creepy received a carrier pigeon message about urgent sect affairs that Ni Laoshan reluctantly stopped, still hungry for more.
Martial arts had been his life's passion. He'd met Zhu Yousheng through a duel and joined the Ghostlight Market initially just to test his skills against its oddball residents. But over time, he'd discovered joys beyond fighting.
"Xiaozhu loves tea, Xiaoba adores wine." As he approached Kaifeng with snacks for his friends, he joked, "They'd better not be mad at me for vanishing for three days."He never imagined he'd return to find them gone, all of them.

Five years passed. Then ten. Then fifteen... Ni Laoshan still wore his carefree grin, but he never dueled again.
In the dead of night, the grin would fall from his face, and he'd stare toward Sleeping Tomb Cemetery.
"Don't worry. This time, I'll guard this place."

挑战最终首领结束后，根据#ffc89c实际战斗时间#E（团灭的战斗时间也会被计入）判断游侠队伍成绩是否可以进入竞速排行榜。若是则发起全员投票表决是否上榜。全员投票同意后将#ffc89c消耗每人一次#E上榜投票次数，并尝试将此次战斗时间上榜。

成功击杀首领的战斗中#ffc89c有队员退出#E会导致无法发起竞速上榜投票。
击败最后首领后，若选择#ffc89c再次挑战#E将无法发起竞速上榜投票。
有队员离开副本或退出队伍时，将视为投票#ffc89c拒绝上榜#E。
之前投票上榜过的队伍，#ffc89c相同队伍成员#E产生更好成绩时将自动更新成绩上榜，#ffc89c不会消耗上榜次数#E。
en:
After defeating the final boss, based on the #ffc89cactual combat#E time (combat time from wipes is also counted), it is determined whether the wanderer team's result can enter the speedrun leaderboard. If so, a vote is initiated among all team members to decide whether to enter the leaderboard. If all team members agree, #ffc89ceach person consumes one#E leaderboard vote attempt, and an attempt is made to post this combat time on the leaderboard.
If any wanderer in the team disagrees, the attempt fails. If the team members have not changed, the leader can #ffc89cinitiate the vote again#E.
To initiate a speedrun leaderboard vote, the team members who defeated each stage boss must #ffc89cremain consistent#E.
If a #ffc89cteammate leaves#E during a successful boss kill, a speedrun leaderboard vote cannot be initiated.
If you choose #ffc89cChallenge Again#E after defeating the final boss, a speedrun leaderboard vote cannot be initiated.
If a teammate leaves the instance or exits the team, it will be considered a #ffc89crefusal to enter the leaderboard#E.
If a team that previously entered the leaderboard achieves a better result with #ffc89cthe same team members#E, the result will automatically update on the leaderboard, #ffc89cwithout consuming a leaderboard attempt#E.

During a heavy snow in Chang'an, the two played beneath a plum tree. A flutist stopped in the snow, joined without a word, and harmony spoke what words could not.

Yaoyao is the youngest of five siblings. 
She is utterly spoiled by the four older ones. That's why she's always smiling, bright-eyed and full of joy. 
One day, she passed the graveyard and heard a human voice. High and stirring one moment, low and tender the next. She didn't know what it meant, only that it was full of... something she couldn't understand. 
Her sister once said: humans love to sing. Was this their singing? 
She wasn't sure, but she wanted to understand. Why did humans sing every day, without ever getting tired? 
Since then, Yaoyao sits by the graveyard daily,
watching the humans "sing" as they come and go, again and again.

Disciples passing the Equilibrium Hall would occasionally see Swallow staring silently at this set of armor.
The armor curls around the body, as if to avoid hearing, seeing, or speaking.
No need to care about genius or ingenuity. No need to mind the flattering or curious gazes of others.
She only wanted to stay quietly in her corner, slowly remembering that first afternoon...
The sun was just right, and the breeze was soft. A dazed little pangolin crawled past the window, opened its sharp scales, and sunned its belly.
The young master's parents watched with tender eyes, smiling as they taught her how to draw shapes from nature.
Then, from a dull piece of wood, it grew into its own shape, carrying the love of her father and mother.

zh:
被罚不让出门的日子里，史三水无聊得要发霉。到睡不着呗
好在，身边还有个蔡小辰陪着。
家里的玩具实在没什么意思，他们拿起大人们的嫖姚棋，一下，一下，弹来弹去。
“听说，赢得人能做将军。嫖姚将军呢！”蔡小辰没头没尾得一句话，史三水都懒得抬头。
“做将军？那我做。我要做最厉害的将军。”史三水摆弄着棋子。
“你做了将军要干什么？”
“干什么都好啊。大将军可以骑马……”史三水拿起骑兵棋。“还可以放大炮！”
“做了大将军，就不能天天跟着阿爷阿娘咯。”蔡小辰拾起旗兵棋。
“唔……那，那你陪我嘛？”史三水抬起头，忽闪忽闪眨着眼睛。
蔡小辰愣了愣。
“那还是我当将军吧。”
“这样，我去打坏人，你就在家等我。” 
“那我多没意思呀！”史三水撇撇嘴。
“我给你带好玩的呀！每次打了胜仗，我都给你买一块玛仁糖。还给你买胡人的好玩意！”
“你就在家，照顾好你阿爷阿娘，也帮我照顾照顾我阿爷阿娘。”
“到时候，你就听着消息。等捷报一传，你得上镇子路口等我。”蔡小辰歪了歪头。“但是别爬那棵树，那树高，你下不来……”
“好，一言为定。”史三水想了想。“那我穿过年的那件红衣裳，这样你很远很远就能看到我。”
“一言为定。”
两只小手拉拉勾，星星月亮和羞走。
en:
During the days they were grounded, Shi Sanshui was bored to death. Couldn't sleep. 
Luckily, Cai Xiaochen was there to keep him company. 
The toys at home were dull. They picked up the adults' Piaoyao Battleboard, flicking the pieces back and forth. 
"They say the winner gets to be a general. Piaoyao General!" Cai Xiaochen's random comment didn't even make Shi Sanshui look up. 
"A general? Then I'll be one. The best general." Shi Sanshui fiddled with a piece. 
"What will you do as a general?" 
"Anything! A general can ride horses..." Shi Sanshui picked up the cavalry piece. "...and fire cannons!" 
"If you become a general, you can't follow your parents around every day," Cai Xiaochen said, picking up the infantry piece. 
"Hmm... Then, will you come with me?" Shi Sanshui looked up, blinking. 
Cai Xiaochen was taken aback. 
"Then maybe I should be the general." 
"That way, I'll fight the bad guys, and you wait for me at home." 
"How boring for me!" Shi Sanshui pouted. 
"I'll bring you cool stuff! After every victory, I'll buy you a piece of walnut brittle. And get you exotic things!" 
"You stay home, take care of your parents, and help take care of mine too." 
"Then, you listen for the news. When word of victory comes, you wait for me at the town crossroads." Cai Xiaochen tilted his head. "But don't climb that tree. It's too tall; you won't get down..." 
"Deal." Shi Sanshui thought for a moment. "I'll wear my red New Year's clothes, so you can see me from far, far away." 
"Deal." 
Two small hands hooked pinkies as stars and the moon shyly slipped away.

zh:
纤阿女的出生，是沙谷深处的隐世村庄里的一桩奇闻。
即使这个村子本身就是个传说，但面对一位以老妪之躯降生的婴孩，众人还是觉得惊骇不已。
村长叹了一口气。“月有圆缺，周而复始。或许她只是比我们更先一步罢了。”
善良的村民们为她捞起一块月亮馍。她尚未长出牙齿，众人只好把馍馍用热水泡软，再一点一点喂给她。

越是强大的波澜，冲击就消散得越快。很快，众人都习惯了这个年幼的老妇人。
纤阿女坐在门槛上，状如痴傻，呆呆地看着村民来来往往。村民们会停下脚步，和善地对她打招呼。
一天，一位少年莽撞地来到她的身边。
“你会捞月亮吗？”少年红扑扑的脸蛋，让纤阿女一愣。她有些慌乱，羞怯地摇了摇头。
“咱们村里的人都会捞月亮，我教你吧！”少年兴冲冲地站起来，拉着纤阿女往清泉中走去。
轻快敏捷的少年忽略了蹒跚学步的腿脚。纤阿女失去重心，却被少年稳稳扶住。
“哥、哥……”纤阿女咿呀着，本能地抓紧少年，一步一步，走向月华正盛的水边。

那一天她还是没有学会怎么捞月亮。即使捞月网轻巧便捷，她也没能找到合适的角度将它丢出去。
但她却记得，那个少年一次一次丢出的捞月网，还有那首朗朗的歌谣。
en:
The birth of Xian'a was a marvel in the hidden village deep within the sandy valley. 
Even though the village itself was something of a legend, facing an infant born in the body of an old woman, everyone was still horrified. 
The village chief sighed. "The moon waxes and wanes, cycles endlessly. Perhaps she is just a step ahead of us." 
Kind villagers scooped up a moon-bun for her. She hadn't yet grown teeth, so they had to soak the bun in hot water until soft and feed it to her bit by bit. 

The stronger the wave, the faster the shock subsides. Soon, everyone grew accustomed to this young old woman. 
Xian'a sat on the doorstep, looking dazed, watching the villagers come and go. They would stop and greet her kindly. 
One day, a boy recklessly came to her side. 
"Do you know how to scoop the moon?" The boy's flushed face startled Xian'a. Flustered and shy, she shook her head. 
"Everyone in our village knows how! I'll teach you!" The boy stood up eagerly, pulling Xian'a towards the clear spring. 
The nimble, agile boy overlooked her unsteady, toddling steps. Xian'a lost her balance but was steadied by the boy's firm hold. 
"Bro... ther..." she babbled, instinctively gripping the boy tightly, step by step walking towards the water brimming with moonlight. 

That day, she still didn't learn how to scoop the moon. Even though the moon-catching net was light and handy, she couldn't find the right angle to throw it. 
But she remembered the net the boy tossed out again and again, and that clear, ringing song.

异香火烛 · 夜鸢

火烛的香气总让她想起很多往事。
她初入墨门时，也和同门弟子一样学做机巧。
夜色下那一豆烛火，总是将自己好不容易搭起的异形木鸢映衬得更加奇形古怪。
左边的翅膀粗壮得像一节枯木，右边的翅膀扁平得像一个煎饼。
反观师父做的那些小玩意儿，轻便好用，妙趣横生。
九折鱼竿、钱坤袋子、还有给封龙弟子做的火折子印章……
她倒是喜欢，可每次自以为思路全了然，做完却又落得个照虎画猫。
好在机巧与武学也有一些相同之处，师父的教导，于习武一道颇有益处。
en:
Fragrant Candle - Night Yuan

The scent of the candle always brings back many memories.
When she first joined the Mohist, she also learned to make mechanisms like the other disciples.
Under the flickering candlelight of the night, her hard-built, strangely shaped Wooden Eagle looked even more bizarre.
The left wing was thick as a dead branch, the right wing flat as a pancake.
In contrast, the little trinkets her master made were light, handy, and full of fun.
A nine-fold fishing rod, a money pouch, and a Fire Striker seal for the disciples...
She liked them, but every time she thought she understood the principle, she ended up drawing a tiger but producing a dog.
Fortunately, mechanisms and martial arts share some similarities. Her master's teachings were quite beneficial to her martial arts practice.

zh:
九流门道主，大侠中的大侠，男人中的男人。
他，沐浴只用冷水，寒冷使他警觉。
他，解渴只用烈酒，醉意让他勇猛。
他不碰甜食，除非孩童殷切递于他手。
他不着彩衣，唯有玄色可匹配他的优雅。
霸道，是他的名字，狂傲，是他的注解。
人们敬他，却也惧他。
无人能走入他的心，也从未有人见识过他的脆弱。
或许某一天，有一人，会终于揭开这江湖最神秘男人的秘密。
谁会是那个人呢？
en:
Dao Lord of Nine Mortal Ways is the grandmaster among grandmasters, the man among men. 
He bathes only in cold water—chill keeps him vigilant. 
He quenches thirst only with strong liquor—drunkenness fuels his valor. 
He avoids sweets unless a child offers them earnestly. 
He wears no bright colors—only obsidian black matches his elegance. 
Domineering is his name, arrogance his epitaph. 
Men revere him, yet fear him too. 
None have entered his heart; none have seen his vulnerability. 
Perhaps one day, someone will unlock the secrets of the martial world's most enigmatic man. 
Who will that person be?

Uncle's message came. Father is gone. To Chang'an.
For Liangzhou, for the Guiyi Army... for everyone, he has offered himself as a hostage.

"It was his own decision," Uncle said.
I don't know what the world looked like when he rode out of that pass.
I only know that the vast lands of Hexi are no longer my home.

Uncle talks of a "wide-open future" for me.
Is this the bargain struck between brothers? One's freedom for the other's fortune?
If my father is the price for that future, I reject the bargain.

A Liangzhou man's fortune is found on his horse and won with his blade.
Uncle himself taught me this. "The sword is nimble, the blade is resolute. The sword dances; the blade strikes true. The way of the blade is to see one path and never stray."

I will claim my own future.

胡三粒记得，父亲还在的时候，每日下午未时便要开始做第二天的豆腐。好的豆腐要经过十道工序。先要在许多黄豆里，挑选出颗粒饱满的豆子。他爹最是实诚，从来不会用坏豆子滥竽充数。一把豆子从他爹手里过去，只有小半能留在篮里。再将这些豆子放在清晨打来的冷泉水里浸泡十几个小时，才能休息一会。
到了子时，其他人都睡下的时候。胡三粒便听到他爹起床磨豆子的声音了。一旦错过了时辰，豆腐就不是这个味了。那时磨出一盆豆子要六个时辰。
二十岁的他喘了口气，抹了抹头上的汗，这是今晚第二件豆腐了。他记得他爹那时候一晚上能做四件豆腐，如今换他来做，却只能做两件了。他的手艺和爹比，究竟差在哪呢？
en:
There's an old saying: among all trades under heaven, three are the hardest, poling boats, hammering iron, and making tofu.
Hu Sanli still remembered how it used to be, back when his father was alive. At early-afternoon, his father would already be preparing the next day's tofu. Making tofu wasn't brute labor, but a careful, fussy work, ten steps from start to finish. The first step alone took patience: picking through mounds of soybeans, choosing only the full, glossy ones. His father was an honest man who never padded the batch with bad beans. A full pile would pass through his hands, and barely half a basket would remain. Even then, the beans had to soak for more than ten hours in cold spring water drawn at dawn. Only after that could he stop and take a break.
At midnight, when the house had fallen into deep sleep, Hu Sanli would hear his father get up to grind the beans. The timing could not be wrong, not even slightly. Miss it, and the tofu would lose its true taste. In those days, grinding a single tub of beans took twelve full hours.
Now, at twenty, Hu Sanli straightened his aching back, drew a breath, and wiped the sweat from his brow. This was his second batch of the night. His father could make four before dawn. He could only manage two. Just where was he lacking in skill compared to his father?

zh:
比武招亲的烂俗戏码，话本里有许多。说，江湖名门侠女，寻不到如意郎君，家中便办上热热闹闹的擂台，要寻那天下第一的才俊做夫婿；又说，街巷内寒女，虽欲卖身葬父，却也不愿嫁于草包，便在街头草草立了个比武招亲的字据，好叫自己也觅一觅江湖知音。这些鸳鸯侠侣、武林恩怨的戏码，幼时的冯如之，喜欢得紧，要追着那编故事的九流门，一口一个“然后呢，然后呢？”然后……很久之后，封丘村的台上，冯如之也办了比武招亲。不是为了什么鸳鸯侠侣、武林恩怨，只为了一个字——钱。

喂饱赤龙堂的姊妹弟兄们要钱，兴修瓠子金堤要钱，给刚成年的堂中孩子们锻刀要钱，给娘亲烧纸钱……也要钱。可朝廷想断了黄河的漕运，钱又不能真从天上来，左思右想，还是得光明正大从过路人的口袋中来。如此，才有这比武招亲的局，一来，赚些赏钱，赢些江湖豪少；二来，多来些喝茱萸汤的商贩，也多些吆喝和买卖；三来，切磋武艺，长些本事，也不枉费这恁多苦心；四来，咳咳……打得多了，便对从前九流门写的话本祛了魅，什么鸳鸯侠侣、武林恩怨，冯如之只觉得俗，简直俗不可耐。什么狗屁情情爱爱，都不如两个铜板儿，实实在在。

可那日，擂台上多了个莽打莽撞，接了绣球的少侠，瞧着甚是眼熟……虽瞧着不是什么达官显贵，不知怎的，却有意思得紧，何妨探探。冯如之戴上傩面，执戈回眸，“下一个？”
en:
There are many stories of marriage contest in storybooks. Some tell of heroic maidens from famous martial arts families who, unable to find a satisfactory husband, hold grand arenas to seek the world's most talented man as their spouse. Others speak of poor girls in the streets who, though forced to sell themselves to bury their fathers, refuse to marry fools, so they hastily post notices for martial arts contests to find kindred spirits in the martial arts world. As a child, Feng Ruzhi loved these tales of knight-errant couples and martial arts grievances. She would chase after the storytellers from the Nine Mortal Ways, asking repeatedly, "And then? And then?" Then… many years later, on the stage of Verdant Hill Village, Feng Ruzhi also held a marriage contest. Not for knight-errant couples or martial arts grievances, but for one thing, money. 

She needed money to feed the brothers and sisters of the Bloodscale Hall, to repair the Huzhi Golden Dyke, to forge swords for the newly adult members of the hall, and to burn paper money for her mother… even that cost money. But the imperial court wanted to cut off the Yellow River's grain transportation, and money didn't fall from the sky. After much thought, she decided to get it openly from passersby. Hence, this marriage contest: first, to earn rewards and win money from wealthy young martial artists; second, to attract more merchants who would drink dogwood soup, bringing more business and commotion; third, to exchange martial arts skills and improve herself, making all this effort worthwhile; fourth, ahem… after fighting so much, she had disillusioned herself with the old storybooks from the Nine Mortal Ways. All that talk of knight-errant couples and martial arts grievances seemed tacky to Feng Ruzhi, downright vulgar. What nonsense love and romance! Nothing was as real as two copper coins. 

But that day, a reckless young hero jumped onto the stage, caught the silk ball, and looked strangely familiar… Though he didn't seem like a noble or wealthy man, there was something intriguing about him. Why not investigate? Feng Ruzhi put on a Nuo mask, held her spear, and turned around: "Next?"

龙何出也，彼人所饲。龙何去也，彼人所屠。
导非其导，堙非其堙。八野疏淤，水去尽也。

en:
Long ago, the Vast Spring surged boundless to the sky.
Before the Xia ruled the land, rivers and mountains had already been claimed. 
The Yellow River was drawn from Jishi, carved through the Dragon Gate. Diverted by the pillars, and guided along its silted banks. 
Where did dragons come from? They were raised by men. Where did dragons go? They were slain by men. 
What was diverted should not have been, what was dammed should not have held. The eight great plains were dredged, and the waters disappeared. 
At Huzi Stream, the waters murmured, and songs rose from Xuanfang. To the River Master who governs the current, we plead you to hold the river in your hand.

zh: 追云，很遗憾，猫不如其名，它不喜欢追云，更喜欢追着人跑。 它伏下身，耳朵转了转，听到熟悉的声音顺着木制的轨道传来。 哐——哐——当啷—— 每当头顶上方的铃声响起时，这里就会下来很多很多人。 到时候它只要打个滚，喵喵两声，就能混到一些鱼干虾米。 偶尔它也会想，云之上有什么好吃的呢，云朵尝起来又是什么样的呢，是白白软软的馒头味，还是冰冰凉凉的雪花味？ 不过，这也不是一只小猫咪应该思考的问题，毕竟填饱肚子才是猫生大事。  追云想到这里，舔了舔爪子，准备睡今天的第三个午觉了。
en:
Cloud Chaser, sadly, does not live up to his name. He doesn't chase clouds.
He chases people. He'd crouch low, ears twitching, listening for that familiar sound along the wooden tracks.
Clank, clank, clatter. When the bell rings overhead, a flood of people would descend. A quick roll, a couple of mews, and he'd score some dried fish or shrimp.
Sometimes, he wonders what clouds might taste like. Soft and white like a steamed bun? Cold and crisp like snow?
But these are not questions for a small cat. Filling his belly is the real business of a cat's life. Satisfied with this thought, he licks his paw and settles in for his third nap of the day.

zh:
来文津馆访学，头一件事——饿了。
寻着饭香摸到膳堂，正是饭点。里头人头攒动，南腔北调混在一处。为最后几勺红烧肉，掏出了扇、笔、刀鞘、剑鞘……各显神通，但都抵不过大娘大爷的大勺，肉落谁家，一勺定音。
一个端盘子的弟子冲我努努嘴：别愣着了，那头还有！
吃饱了出来，到处溜达。
这头松风居，一位师弟蹲门口补袜子，针脚歪歪扭扭，路过的师兄看不过眼：“唉……我来！”那头沧浪居，师妹对着书本点头如捣蒜，旁边的师姐扶额叹气：“唉……我来！”浩然苑那边也热闹，一对青年男女正对着彼此放狠话，发誓下次考评定要超过对方，中气十足。
旁边还有好大一片蹴鞠场，散步的，跑步的，打太极的，在杠上旋转如风的……各忙各的。那边还有几个弟子颠球，一脚下去，球飞了……径直栽进洗砚池，墨花四溅。
池边正蹲着七八个人涮笔砚。一位弟子刚把砚台拎起来，对着太阳鉴宝似的端详……不幸被溅了一身“墨水”。那人追着球过来，忙着道歉，洗砚台那位笑眯眯的，回敬了他一抔墨。
洗砚池边上便是静室，门一关，连翻书声都听得见。我蹑手蹑脚退开，回到憩室。有人歪着翻闲书，有人凑在窗边低声聊江湖八卦，角落还摆着酒壶……看来这八卦是下酒得很！
这地方，好像没太多规矩。什么人都有，什么人都自在。歇着的，玩着的，学着的……千姿百态，各得其所，像个浓缩的小小江湖。
不同的是，这里透着外头难得的松弛与从容。个个都像抖擞羽毛、晾晒翅根的小雀，大概是都在鲲鹏的羽翼之下。
嗨呀，年轻真好。
en:
The first order of business upon arriving to study at the Inkbound Order was sating my hunger.
Following the scent of food, I found my way to the Dining Hall just in time for the meal. The place was packed, dialects from all directions mixing together. For the last few scoops of braised pork, people whipped out fans, brushes, blade sheaths, sword sheaths. Each showed off their own tricks, but none could outmatch the aunties' and uncles' ladles. Wherever the meat landed, that ladle had the final say.
A disciple with a plate in his hand urged me, "Quit idling, there's more over there!"
Once full, I went out and wandered around.
At Pine Breeze Lodge, a junior brother crouched by the door mending his socks, stitches crooked and uneven; a passing senior brother couldn't stand it. "Ugh... let me do it!"
At Canglang Lodge, a junior sister nodded over her book like she was pounding garlic, while the senior sister beside her sighed and rubbed her temples. "Ugh... let me do it!"
Over at Noble Courtyard, things were lively too. A young man and woman traded trash talk with full lungs, each vowing to outscore the other in the next evaluation.
Beside it lay a huge Cuju field, with people strolling, jogging, practicing Tai Chi, spinning like the wind atop the bars... everyone busy with their own thing. Over there, a few disciples were juggling a ball. One kick sent it flying... straight into the inkstone-washing pond, splattering ink everywhere.
By the pond, several people crouched, rinsing brushes and inkstones. One disciple had just picked up an inkstone, examining it against the sun like appraising a treasure... only to be unluckily splashed head to toe with "ink water." The ball-chaser rushed over, hastily apologizing, while the inkstone-washer grinned and flicked a handful of ink right back at him.
Next to the inkstone-washing pond was the quiet study room. Once the door shut, you could even hear the rustle of turning pages. I tiptoed away and returned to the resting room. Some lounged about reading casual books, others leaned by the window murmuring about Jianghu gossip, and in the corner sat a wine jug... seems this gossip pairs quite well with drink!
This place doesn't seem to have too many rules. All sorts of people here, each at ease in their own way. Some resting, some playing, some studying... a hundred different postures, each finding their place, like a miniature Jianghu condensed into one.
The difference is, this place carries a rare sense of ease and calm you don't find outside. Everyone looks like a little sparrow preening its feathers and drying its wings, perhaps all sheltered beneath the wings of some great roc.
Ah, how nice it is to be young.
Ye Ling Qiu

zh: 《礼记》成于先秦至西汉，乃孔门弟子及后学记礼之文汇编。原为附经之记，单篇别行。西汉戴德删古文《记》为八十五篇，称《大戴礼记》；其从子戴圣复删为四十九篇，称《小戴礼记》。后者汉末郑玄作注，遂与《周礼》《仪礼》合称“三礼”，且自唐列为五经之一。其文分通论、制度、丧服、吉礼、祭法、乐记、明堂诸类，所涉礼义、典制、教育、修身、乐论、政事，尤以《礼运》《学记》《乐记》《王制》《月令》《儒行》诸篇影响深远，其中《大学》《中庸》二篇，尤为后世理学家所重。唐孔颖达奉诏修《礼记正义》，定为官学取士之本。
en: The Book of Rites was compiled from the pre-Qin era through to the Western Han, and is an assemblage of writings on ritual recorded by the Disciples of Confucius and their successors. Originally composed as supplementary records appended to the classics, the individual chapters circulated separately. In the Western Han, Dai De abridged the Old Text Records into eighty-five chapters, known as the Elder Dai's Record of Rites; his nephew Dai Sheng further abridged them into forty-nine chapters, known as the Lesser Dai Book of Rites. The latter received a commentary by Zheng Xuan in the late Han, whereupon it came to be known together with the Rites of Zhou and the Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial as the "Three Rites," and from the Tang dynasty onward was listed among the Five Classics. Its contents are divided into such categories as general discourses, institutional regulations, mourning garments, auspicious rites, sacrificial laws, music records, and the hall of light. Its subjects encompass ritual and righteousness, canonical institutions, education, self-cultivation, discourse on music, and statecraft. Of particular far-reaching influence are the chapters on the Conveyance of Rites, the Record of Learning, the Record of Music, the Rule of Kings, the Monthly Ordinances, and the Conduct of the Confucian. Among these, the two chapters of the Great Learning and the Doctrine of the Mean were held in especial esteem by later scholars of the Learning of Principle. zh:
古乐这名字，取得好也不好。
一个乐字，好像就预言了他一生的宿命，这辈子都与琴脱不开关系。

从始至终，古乐只有一个愿望。他喜欢抚琴，将琴弹给很多人听。山间的樵夫、路边的老妇、牙牙学语的孩童，奇异的是，不管什么样的人，都静静地听懂了他的琴，并对他回以微笑。
人们说，这是古乐的特异，能弹出所有人都听懂的声音。
所以他就一直那么弹着，直到有一天，他发现人们不再来听他的琴。
人们不再微笑了，惊慌的表情取而代之。人们也不再停留了，只会匆匆地掠过他身边，耳朵都被哭泣和呼喊声堵上，听不进别的。

古乐茫然地望向人们想要逃离的方向，滚滚硝烟被隆隆的铁蹄踏起。
原来战争起时，人们听不进任何乐声。
于是他收起琴，握住向他伸出的手，加入了抗击契丹的队伍。和队中的那群人一起，有了后来河东八俊的名号。

毕竟，从始至终，古乐只有一个愿望。
en:
The name Gu Le is both fitting and ironic.
The character "le", meaning "music," seems to have foretold his destiny: a life inseparable from the lute.

From start to finish, Gu Le had only one wish: to play the lute for as many people as possible. Woodcutters in the mountains, old women by the roadside, toddlers learning to speak. Strangely, no matter who they were, they all listened silently to his music and smiled in return.
People said he had a gift: the ability to play sounds that everyone could understand.
So he played on until the day the crowds ceased to gather.
The smiles vanished, replaced by panic. No one lingered anymore. They rushed past, their ears deaf to all but screams and sobs.

Gu Le stared blankly in the direction they fled, where billowing smoke rose to the thunder of iron hooves.
War had come, and in its shadow, no one could hear music.
So he packed away his lute, took the hand extended to him, and joined the fight against the Khitan. Alongside those comrades, he would later be known as one of the Eight Talents of Hedong.

After all, from beginning to end, Gu Le had but one wish.

en:
...
The word "love" is unfathomable, like mirrors reflecting one another, or dreams spawning within dreams.
It is hard to glimpse its form, hard to touch its substance, hard to break its illusions, and hard to comprehend its logic. So many foolish men and women have been buried in the sea of passion, leaving no bones behind.
The tale recounted here also struggles to escape this tragic mold... In the end, it is but seeking fruit from an illusory flower, or chasing fish in a mirage. ... If one asks where love begins, and where it ultimately ends?
It is exactly thus: A single drop in the sea of passion breeds chaotic clouds on the path of karma; when destiny ends, it concludes in falling tears, leaving only empty seafoam on the shores of the afterlife.

zh:
贞明三年，三月七日
初次出山，长老命我需挣得白银五十两。
……五十两！需三口之家，数年辛劳，殊为不易。甚愁。
贞明三年，三月八日

贞明三年，三月九日。
路遇劫匪，缴得二两二钱。

贞明三年，三月十日
路遇劫匪，缴得七两八钱。

贞明三年，三月十一日
一日竟三遇劫匪！噫！天下之乱，扼腕而叹。

贞明三年，三月十二日
又遇劫匪。细数怀中银钱，竟已存二十有余，距五十两近半矣。
莫不如再寻劫匪一番。勿思，勿思。我等墨门弟子，岂可堕于劫财？
贞明三年，三月十三日
偶遇劫匪，得钱三两。匪徒如蚁，避无可避，非我刻意寻之。

贞明三年，三月十四日
遇契丹马匪窜劫关内，满载膏梁锦绣，缴得白银四十九两！
悲，我所学这一身技艺，当真无用矣？
贞明三年，三月十五日
寻得数名契丹马匪，得银二十两，唾之，穷鬼。

贞明三年，三月十六日
遍寻契丹马匪不可得？叹曰，吾堕矣。

贞明三年，三月十七日
至滹沱河，见百马凿蹄，千弓空鸣，原是契丹马匪围杀侠客三人。
快哉！此番定能缴得银两逾百！
贞明三年，三月十八日
我所学技艺终有用武之地。那侠客三人以白银五十两，请我于滹沱河上搭桥一座。
贞明三年，三月十九日
今日方知，侠客三人名为徐知诰、王清、李无心。
不妙，天下纷争不入墨门。此番际遇，万不可让长老获悉。
en:
7th day of the Third Month, Year 3 of Zhenming
My first day down the mountain. The Elder ordered me to earn fifty taels of silver.
...Fifty taels! A family of three could labor for years and not save such a sum. I am deeply troubled.

8th day of the Third Month, Year 3 of Zhenming
Encountered bandits on the road. Levied one tael and three qian.

9th day of the Third Month, Year 3 of Zhenming
Encountered bandits on the road. Levied two taels and two qian.

10th day of the Third Month, Year 3 of Zhenming
Encountered bandits on the road. Levied seven taels and eight qian.

11th day of the Third Month, Year 3 of Zhenming
Three encounters with bandits in a single day! Alas! The chaos of this world leaves one sighing in despair.

12th day of the Third Month, Year 3 of Zhenming
Met bandits again. Counting the silver in my pouch, I have amassed over twenty taels, nearly half my goal.
Perhaps I should seek out more bandits. No, no. As disciples of Mohist Hill, how can we stoop to highway robbery?

13th day of the Third Month, Year 3 of Zhenming
Chanced upon bandits. Gained three taels. The rogues are like ants; I cannot avoid them even if I try. I am certainly not seeking them out.

14th day of the Third Month, Year 3 of Zhenming
Intercepted Khitan horse thieves plundering inside the pass, their packs heavy with fine silks. Levied forty-nine taels of silver!
Oh, the tragedy. Is the martial craft I honed truly reduced to this?

15th day of the Third Month, Year 3 of Zhenming
Tracked down a few more Khitan horse thieves. Got twenty taels. I spit on them. Paupers.

16th day of the Third Month, Year 3 of Zhenming
Searched everywhere for Khitan thieves but found none. I sighed. I have fallen from grace.

17th day of the Third Month, Year 3 of Zhenming
Arrived at the Hutuo River. Hundreds of horses stamping their hooves, thousands of bows drawn tight. It was a horde of Khitan bandits laying siege to three wandering martial artists.
Excellent! This haul will surely net me over a hundred taels!

18th day of the Third Month, Year 3 of Zhenming
My sect's skills finally proved their worth. Those three martial artists paid me fifty taels of silver to build a bridge across the Hutuo River for them.

19th day of the Third Month, Year 3 of Zhenming
Only today did I learn the names of those three: Xu Zhigao, Wang Qing, and Li Wuxin.
This is terrible. Mohist Hill strictly forbids involvement in worldly conflicts. The Elder must never learn of this encounter.

Their aim is to exploit public outrage over the policy of confiscating Tang Coin, driving a wedge between Zhao court officials and the people, and halting the southern campaign. 杜乾从小就喜欢钱。废话，谁不喜欢钱？
但杜乾格外喜欢。爹娘花了好大的力气，打骂齐上，才让杜乾知道别人的钱不能拿，偷抢骗都不行。
那还有什么来钱快的法子？杜乾日日琢磨。看这法条上，也没写管的范围，这什么官差也没见过啊？
杜乾开始按着法条尝试。用一块石子，换了小妹妹的糖葫芦；设局和别人赌了五个钱，当晚就收回了二十个。
杜乾发现自己可能是坑蒙拐骗的天才，但爹娘的谆谆教诲让他半夜给人小妹妹又送了一串糖葫芦回去。
他苦思冥想。骗好人的钱叫坑蒙拐骗，骗坏人的钱叫劫富济贫。
看着破门村不知从哪来了一堆江湖人，杜乾打定主意支起了赌棋摊。
江湖人，不一定是好人；赌局，也不一定会赢啊！
杜乾自洽了。
挣钱嘛，不寒碜！
en:
Du Qian had loved money for as long as he could remember. Well... who didn't?
The difference was that he loved it a little too much. His parents tried everything, beatings, scoldings, and lectures, before finally drilling one rule into his head: other people's money was off-limits. No stealing. No robbing. No cheating.
Which left him with a problem. If all that was forbidden, then what was the fastest way he was allowed to make money? Du Qian mulled it over day after day. The law books didn't say how far their jurisdiction went. And officials? Never seen one.
So he began to test the edges. A pebble traded for his little sister's Candied Hawthorn. A rigged game here, five coins in, twenty back by nightfall.
It dawned on Du Qian that he might be gifted at this sort of thing. Still, his parents' words echoed too loudly, so under the cover of the night, he returned a fresh Candied Hawthorn to the little girl he'd tricked.
He thought harder about it. Tricking good people was fraud. Tricking bad people, though, that was taking from the rich to help the poor.
Then a crowd of wanderers drifted into Brokegate Village. Du Qian made up his mind and set up a gambling board.
Wanderers weren't necessarily good people, and gambling didn't always mean winning, right?
Logic intact.
Making money isn't shabby work!

zh:
夜深了，天工阁内仍灯火通明。
“邹师兄，还不走啊，早点休息啊。”路过的师弟关切道。
“邹师兄还在改论文呢，别打扰他了。”一旁的另一人低声劝阻。
“邹师兄，我先走了，钥匙给你放老位置了，记得关门。”
邹师兄笑笑，温声应下。
邹师兄不是墨门的大师兄，甚至连内门弟子都不是，他只是一个普通的外门弟子。但提起邹师兄，上到长老，下到阿旺，无人不夸邹师兄的好。
无他，只因他待人至诚。无论什么事，只要找邹师兄帮忙，他都尽心尽力，从不推诿。
然而这样的人，却有个记了他十七年的 “仇人”。
说仇人也不全对，杨千言从不主动提邹易州。他们俩只是默契地避开所有相见的场合。
故而无人知晓，莘野坊不务正业卖话本子的杨千言，与外门弟子中最受人欢迎的邹师兄，曾是知交挚友。

十七年前，碧水云涛的桃花林还没像如今这般繁盛。
春三月，桃枝斜斜探向水面，嫩红的花苞缀在枝头，像绿绸上的胭脂碎。
十六岁的邹易州背着半旧的书箧，鞋尖沾着晨露打湿的青草，正往林深处走，忽听得一阵吟诵声从高处飘来，清朗朗的：“东风吹醒桃花雨，明月照彻碧水波。”
他脚步顿了顿，循着声音抬头看过去，见个瘦高的少年坐在桃树上，青布衫洗得发了白，袖口磨出了毛边，手里攥着卷泛黄的诗稿。少年听见脚步声抬头，见了他，只扬了扬手里的稿子，笑着问：“你也喜欢诗？”
邹易州原本想拱手作揖，“在下邹易州……”
不成想他这一弯腰，书箧里探出头了只小山猪。那小山猪眨了眨眼睛，三俩下拱出了书箧，跳了下来，一溜烟跑走了。
“哈哈哈哈——” 书上的少年连声大笑，“竟有人书箧里不装书，装的是只山猪！妙人，真是妙人！”
笑完，他轻巧跳了下来，也拱手回礼，见指尖还沾着墨渍，便随手蹭在长衫下摆上。“在下杨千言。刚凑了两句闲诗，让邹兄和猪兄……噗嗤，都见笑了。”
邹易州望着跑远的小山猪，又看了看笑得直不起腰的杨千言，忙解释道：“原本是我怕它闯祸，才暂时放进书箧里……” 话没说完，倒被自己逗乐了 —— 好好的书箧成了 “猪窝”，确实荒唐。
杨千言笑够了，拍了拍他的肩，眼里满是兴味：“管它装书还是装猪，能把山猪藏进书箧的，邹兄是头一个。” 他晃了晃手里的诗稿，“刚念的两句还没写完，邹兄看着也懂诗，帮我推敲推敲？”
墨门封山千载，人人皆崇尚机巧，诗词歌赋反倒少有人读。因而两人一见如故。
邹易州说，他于机巧一事无甚天赋，却爱写些话本传奇，精怪志异。怕被夫子发现，便在写话本时改了个笔名。结果还是被发现了，说是不务正业。杨千言说，正巧，我也是个机巧白丁，连夫子都不肯收我。只会写些酸诗。这样，以后邹兄尽可以拿我的名字去写话本，我不怕。我还能给你写诗，写批语。
日头偏西时，邹易州见小山猪还未回来，有些着急。
杨千言拉着他往林外走：“别急，我刚才瞧见它往南边去了，那地方有嫩草，准在那儿。”
果然，两人在田边的土坡上找到了猪兄 —— 它正蜷在暖阳里打盹，嘴角还沾着草屑。邹易州上前轻轻抱起它，小山猪哼唧了两声，竟往他怀里蹭了蹭。杨千言站在一旁看着，忽然笑道：“邹兄，这传奇志异的故事，我看第一篇就得是这山猪。”
说完两人哈哈大笑。

自那以后，桃林便成了两人常来之处。
他们说等开山以后，要游遍河山，像当年的李杜，元白，一人写一人和。
他们还约定，以后要一起在山外开个书社。
“听说开封城最热闹，咱们到时候就把书社开在最热闹的街口，门口种上两株从山里带出去的桃树！” 杨千言在誊抄最新的话本。他俩的书已经在山中风靡开了。
邹易州笑着点头，指尖在纸上写下 “千金不易” 四个字，“那书社的牌匾，就挂这四个字。”
杨千言的千，邹易州的易。
千帆一舟，千金不易。
那时的他们还年少，以为这样的日子还有很多，以为碧水云涛的桃花明年还会再开，以为两人会一起把故事写尽，以为那只小山猪会长成大山猪的样子。
那是十七年前的春三月。
后来，有人从天工阁角落里寻到几本破旧不堪的话本子，题诗之人是杨千言。有几页，还夹着几根猪鬃毛。
有弟子拿着书去问这书是谁的，“邹师兄，这杨千言是何人啊……你见过吗？”
“见过的，很久以前。”
en:
The night had deepened, yet Divinecraft Pavilion remained brightly lit. 
"Senior Brother Zou, still here? You should get some rest," a passing junior called out with concern. 
"He's still revising his paper—let's not disturb him," another whispered softly. 
"Senior Brother Zou, I'm heading off. I left the key where I always do. Don't forget to lock up." 
Zou smiled warmly in reply. 
Zou isn't the head disciple of the Mohist Hill. In fact, he's not even a core disciple, just an ordinary outer one. Still, whenever his name comes up, everyone from the elders to Buster speaks highly of him. 
The reason was simple: he treated everyone with sincere kindness. No matter the request, if anyone sought his help, Zou gave his all—never hesitant, never turning anyone away. 
But even a man like him had someone he'd been estranged from for seventeen years. 
Though calling it hatred was too strong—Yang never spoke of Zou, and the two quietly avoided each other whenever chance might bring them face to face. 
What no one knew was that Yang, the carefree storyteller, and Zou, the most admired senior among outer disciples, had once been inseparable friends. 

Seventeen years ago, the peach grove by the sparkling waters of Jadestream Valley had yet to bloom into the lush sea of blossoms it is now. 
In early spring, peach branches stretched gently over the water, their delicate pink buds like scattered rouge on vibrant green silk. 
Sixteen-year-old Zou walked deeper into the forest, a worn book satchel slung over his shoulder, his shoes damp from the morning dew kissing the grass beneath his feet. Suddenly, a clear, melodious voice drifted down from above:
"The east wind wakes the peach blossom rain,
The bright moon lights the jade-green waves." 
He paused, lifted his gaze, and spotted a slender youth perched among the branches of a peach tree. His faded blue shirt was worn thin and frayed at the cuffs, and he clutched a yellowed scroll of poetry. Catching sight of Zou, the boy smiled and raised the scroll. "You like poetry too?" 
Zou bowed politely, about to introduce himself. "I am Zou Yizhou…" 
But as he bent forward, a tiny wild boar poked its snout from the satchel. Blinking its bright eyes, the little creature clumsily scrambled free and darted off into the woods. 
The boy burst into laughter. "Hahaha! Who hides a wild piglet inside their book satchel instead of books? Truly one of a kind!" 
His laughter ringing through the grove, the boy gracefully leapt down, returning Zou's bow with a playful grin. Noticing ink stains on his fingertips, he casually wiped them on the hem of his robe. "I'm Yang Qianyan. Just tossing together a few stray lines of poetry. Looks like I've made fools of both you and your piglet friend." 
Zou watched the boar disappear into the underbrush, then glanced back at Yang, who was still chuckling. He hurried to explain, "I only tucked it in the satchel to keep it from running wild..." He couldn't help but laugh too—the idea of a book satchel turned pigsty was absurdly charming. 
When the laughter settled, Yang clapped him on the shoulder with genuine warmth. "Whether it's books or boars, you're the first I've known to carry a wild pig in a satchel." He waved the scroll playfully. "Those lines I just read aren't finished yet. You seem to have an ear for poetry—care to help me refine them?" 
For a thousand years, the Mohist Hill disciples prized mechanical ingenuity above all else—poetry, prose, and song had fallen into neglect. Because of this, the two young men connected instantly, as if old friends reunited. 
Zou confessed he lacked any real talent for mechanics but found joy in writing tales of legends, strange creatures, and the supernatural. To keep this secret from their master, he adopted a pen name. Still, he was caught and scolded for neglecting his proper duties. Yang laughed and said, "Funny enough, I'm a complete novice when it comes to mechanics, and even the master wouldn't take me in. All I do is write bitter little poems. If you want, you can use my name for your stories—I don't mind. I can even craft poems and notes to accompany them." 
As the sun dipped westward, Zou grew anxious—the little wild boar had yet to return. 
Yang took his hand and led him toward the forest's edge. "Don't worry—I saw it wander south earlier. There's fresh grass there; it's probably resting nearby." 
Sure enough, they found the boar curled in a patch of warm sunlight on a hillside by the fields, dozing with bits of grass stuck at its mouth. Zou gently lifted the creature, which softly snuffled and nestled against his chest. Watching this, Yang smiled and said, "Zou, I believe your first tale of legends should be about this wild boar." 
They laughed together, their joy echoing through the grove. 

From that day on, the peach grove became their treasured refuge. 
They dreamed of the day the mountain would reopen, when they could journey across the land like the great poets of old—one writing verses, the other composing replies. 
And they vowed to open a bookstore beyond the mountain, a place where their stories and poems could live and breathe, together. 
"I've heard Kaifeng City is the liveliest place around," Yang said as he copied out the latest manuscript. "When the time comes, let's open our bookstore right at the busiest street corner—and plant two peach trees at the doorway, ones we bring all the way from the mountains." Their stories had already become wildly popular deep within the mountains. 
Zou smiled and nodded, then penned four characters on the paper: Qian Jin Bu Yi—"Priceless and Rare." "That will be the sign above our shop." 
The "Qian" from Yang, the "Yi" from Zou. 
Together in one boat, priceless and rare. 
They were young then, believing such days would stretch on forever—that the peach blossoms by the crystal-clear Jadestream Valley would bloom again next spring—that they would share countless stories side by side—that the little wild boar would one day grow into a mighty beast. 
That was the spring seventeen years ago. 
Later, a few weathered, fragile scripts were found tucked away in a forgotten corner of Divinecraft Pavilion. The poems inside bore the name Yang Qianyan, and pressed between the pages were a few strands of boar's bristles. 
One disciple held the books and asked, "Senior Brother Zou, who exactly is this Yang Qianyan? Have you met him?" 
"I have. Long ago."
Huh? Do I have a hole in my pocket?
